Kiro & ABAP Accelerator for SAP

A hands-on workshop for SAP ABAP developers to accelerate clean core adoption (extending SAP without modifying the core) using AWS's agentic AI IDE Kiro with the ABAP Accelerator MCP server for code generation, modernization, and troubleshooting on AWS.

By Nonthakorn Junthapol · SAP Specialist SA · AWS

3–4 Hours Intermediate 8 Modules 15 Labs Updated 2026-10-06

How it works

Kiro never edits your SAP system directly. It talks to it through the open Model Context Protocol: the ABAP Accelerator MCP server (a free Docker image) exposes ~15 tools that use the ADT APIs to browse, create, syntax-check, run ATC, and activate objects — so generated code is checked and remediated before it lands. Your SAP system can run in a customer-managed AWS account (you own and operate it) or a SAP-managed account under RISE with SAP — either way Kiro reaches it only through the Accelerator over ADT, never directly.In RISE with SAP, developers still write ABAP in ADT (ABAP Development Tools) over that same ADT connection — Kiro and the Accelerator sit alongside it, not in place of it.Source: AWS for SAP blog, “Introducing the ABAP Accelerator”, Jan 2026.

Module 1: Introduction & Setup (30 minutes)

Learning Objectives

  • Understand what Kiro offers for SAP ABAP development
  • Set up the complete development environment from scratch
Before You Begin (please set up ahead of the session)

To keep hands-on time productive, please complete this before the session:

  • Set up Kiro — the agentic IDE used throughout this workshop.
  • Confirm your SAP user has a developer role — S_DEVELOP or equivalent authorization. ABAP writing/development exercises will not work without it.

If you can't set this up beforehand, that's OK — we'll allocate 30 minutes at the start of the day to do it together.

1.1 What is Kiro?

Kiro is an agentic AI IDE from AWS that goes beyond code completion. It uses spec-driven development to turn natural language prompts into structured requirements, system designs, and implementation tasks. Key features:

  • Spec-driven development — Turns prompts into requirements, design, and tasks before writing code
  • Agent hooks — Automate tasks like generating docs and tests on file save
  • Steering files — Configure clean core standards and preferred workflows per project
  • Built on Code OSS — Familiar VS Code experience, import your existing settings and extensions
  • Native MCP support — Connect to SAP directly (e.g., the AWS ABAP Accelerator MCP server) to read code, validate against ATC, and generate clean core artifacts

Why Kiro: Kiro is AWS’s recommended agentic IDE — inline chat, agentic multi-step coding, native MCP, terminal integration, and spec-driven development. This workshop uses Kiro throughout.

How AWS frames AI in SAP development: assisted → autonomous → driven

As you use these tools, it helps to know where they sit on AWS's spectrum for AI in SAP development:

  • AI-assisted: AI helps with isolated tasks (code completion, explanation, documentation), but you drive the overall process. Most of this workshop's labs work this way.
  • AI-autonomous: AI is handed full control. This tends to break down against the complexity of enterprise SAP systems.
  • AI-driven: AI initiates the workflow, proposes plans and code, and asks for your approval at each decision point, while you keep oversight. This is the direction AWS now recommends for SAP ABAP, formalized in AWS's AI-Driven Development Lifecycle (AI-DLC) methodology (introduced 2025) and applied to SAP ABAP with Kiro + ABAP Accelerator (AWS for SAP guidance, June 2026).

You'll practice AI-assisted patterns throughout; keep the AI-driven model in mind as the target operating mode for real projects. See the AI-DLC for SAP ABAP walkthrough ↗

1.2 Supported ABAP Patterns

Kiro understands:

  • Classical ABAP (reports, module pools, function modules)
  • ABAP Objects (classes, interfaces)
  • CDS views and ABAP annotations
  • RAP (RESTful ABAP Programming Model) — the clean core, on-stack extension model
  • CAP (Cloud Application Programming Model) — for side-by-side extensions on SAP BTP
  • ALV programming (classical and OO)
  • SAP-specific tables, BAPIs, released APIs, and transactions

1.3 Your IDE: Kiro

This workshop uses Kiro, AWS’s agentic AI IDE, as the single development environment. Kiro provides inline chat and code suggestions, agentic multi-step coding, spec-driven development, agent hooks, and native MCP support for the ABAP Accelerator — the capabilities the hands-on labs rely on. Set it up next.

Hands-On Lab 1.3: Configure Kiro for ABAP Development

Model selection: In the Kiro Chat model selector, choose Claude Opus 5 (or the current top-tier Claude Opus model available in your Kiro plan) for the best ABAP generation quality. The default lighter model is fine for simple prompts, but Opus produces noticeably better RAP artifacts, clean-core refactoring, and multi-object reasoning.

Step 1: Create a steering file for ABAP standards

  1. Open your project folder in Kiro
  2. Create .kiro/steering/abap.md with this content:
# ABAP Clean Core Development Standards

## Clean Core Principles
- Never modify SAP standard objects — extend, don't modify
- Consume RELEASED APIs and released CDS views only (check the API state)
- Prefer on-stack extensions with ABAP Cloud / RAP, or side-by-side on SAP BTP (CAP)
- Keep the digital core upgrade-stable and cloud-compliant

## Coding Standards
- Follow Clean ABAP guidelines
- Use modern ABAP syntax (inline declarations, string templates, NEW operator)
- No SELECT * — always use explicit field lists
- No SELECT inside LOOP — use JOINs or FOR ALL ENTRIES
- Use CL_SALV_TABLE for ALV output (not REUSE_ALV_*)
- Use RETURNING parameters instead of CHANGING where possible

## Naming Conventions
- Local variables: lv_, lt_, ls_, lo_, lr_, lx_
- Global variables: gv_, gt_, gs_, go_
- Parameters: iv_, it_, is_, io_ (importing), ev_, et_ (exporting), rv_, rt_ (returning)
- Classes: zcl_ prefix
- Interfaces: zif_ prefix

## SAP Version
- Target: S/4HANA 2023 or later (Cloud Private or Public Edition)
- Use released APIs where possible for clean core compliance

Kiro — File Explorer

Expected: Your steering file (e.g., .kiro/steering/abap.md) is saved, and Kiro references the clean-core rules in its answers.

Object-naming conventions (reference)

The steering file above pins variable prefixes. For repository objects, give Kiro this table too so every generated artifact lands with a predictable, upgrade-stable name. These follow SAP's RAP / Virtual Data Model conventions — adapt the Z namespace to your own (Z/Y or a registered /NAMESPACE/).

ObjectConventionExample
Development packageZ_<AREA> (structure/transportable)Z_SALES_APP
CDS interface view (basic/reuse)ZI_<Entity>ZI_SalesOrderItem
CDS restricted reuse viewZR_<Entity>ZR_SalesOrderItemTP
CDS consumption / projection viewZC_<Entity>ZC_SalesOrderItem
Behavior definition (BDEF)same name as the root entity it definesZR_SalesOrderItemTP
Service definitionZUI_<Area> / ZAPI_<Area>ZUI_SALESORDER
Service binding (OData V4)service-def name + _O4ZUI_SALESORDER_O4
Classzcl_zcl_sales_order_reader
Interfacezif_zif_sales_order_source
Local variables / tables / structures / refslv_ / lt_ / ls_ / lo_ / lr_ / lx_lt_sales_orders
Transport requestno prefix — describe the change in the request text; the agent never releases it (see the Governed AI Development module)“Sales order item CDS + RAP service”

Connect to SAP (MCP)

Point Kiro at your SAP system now, so every module that follows works on your real objects. Kiro reaches SAP through the ABAP Accelerator MCP server (read & validate over ADT). Follow the full setup below — once it says Connected, ask Kiro to read a program or table and your live SAP data appears in chat.

Time: 10 minutes

Objective

Install an SAP ABAP MCP server and connect it to your IDE so Kiro can read SAP objects directly.

Prerequisites

  • Python 3.9+ installed (python3 --version to check)
  • Access to an SAP system with ADT services enabled
  • SAP username, password, client number, and system URL

Steps

Step 1 — Clone and install the MCP server:

git clone https://github.com/YahorNovik/mcp-adt.git
cd mcp-adt
python3 -m venv .venv
source .venv/bin/activate
pip install -r requirements.txt

Step 2 — Configure the SAP connection (securely):

Credential security — do not ship a plaintext password

A password typed into a committed .env is fine only for a throwaway laptop demo. For any customer or shared environment, harden it:

  • Prefer token auth — no stored password. For cloud ABAP (SAP BTP) use SAP_AUTH_TYPE=jwt with a short-lived SAP_JWT_TOKEN (Option A). The server can generate the config straight from a BTP service key (btp_env_generator.py), so no password is written by hand.
  • If you must use basic auth (Option B), use a dedicated, least-privilege, non-dialog technical user (these are read tools — a read-only user covers most labs), and pull the password from a secret store (AWS Secrets Manager / SAP Credential Store / OS keychain), injected at runtime — never a committed file.
  • Keep TLS verification on (SAP_VERIFY_SSL=true); add SNC on-prem where available.
  • git-ignore .env and chmod 600 it; rotate the password after the event.
  • On AWS, store the secret in Secrets Manager and let the launch script write the env at boot (see the Workshop Studio build kit) — never bake credentials into an image or repo.
  • Sign in to Kiro itself with enterprise identity (IAM Identity Center), separate from the SAP service user.

Pick the auth mode your system supports. Option A (token) is preferred; Option B (basic) is for on-prem systems without BTP token auth.

Option A — BTP / cloud ABAP, JWT (recommended):

# .env  —  Option A: BTP / cloud ABAP, JWT token (no password stored)
SAP_AUTH_TYPE=jwt
SAP_URL=https://your-system.abap.<region>.hana.ondemand.com
SAP_JWT_TOKEN=   # short-lived token; inject at runtime, do not commit
SAP_VERIFY_SSL=true

# Generate it from a BTP service key without hardcoding a password:
# python btp_env_generator.py --service-key service-key.json \
#     --username you@example.com --prompt-password

Option B — on-prem, basic auth with a least-privilege user:

# .env  —  Option B: on-prem, basic auth. Do NOT hardcode SAP_PASS.
SAP_AUTH_TYPE=basic
SAP_URL=https://your-sap-system:443
SAP_CLIENT=100
SAP_USER=ZKIRO_RO            # dedicated least-privilege, non-dialog user
SAP_VERIFY_SSL=true

# Inject the password at runtime from a secret store (not in this file):
# export SAP_PASS="$(aws secretsmanager get-secret-value \
#     --secret-id kiro/sap/dev --query SecretString --output text)"

Either way, keep the file out of Git and locked down:

echo ".env" >> .gitignore   # never commit the connection file
chmod 600 .env                 # restrict to your user

Step 3 — Test the connection:

# Quick test — curl PROMPTS for the password instead of exposing it
# in shell history / the process list (never put it in the command).
curl -u YOUR_USER https://your-sap-system:443/sap/bc/adt/discovery

Step 4 — Register the server in Kiro:

Add it to ~/.kiro/settings/mcp.json. If you run the official ABAP Accelerator (a local HTTP server on port 8000, the setup used in this workshop), register it by URL — this is the recommended path:

Sub-steps of Step 4 — do these in order:

  1. Open the MCP config. Command palette (Cmd+Shift+P / Ctrl+Shift+P) → Kiro: Open user MCP config (JSON) for a global server (~/.kiro/settings/mcp.json, applies to all projects), or Kiro: Open workspace MCP config (JSON) for this project only (.kiro/settings/mcp.json). You can also open it from the Kiro panel → MCP Servers → Open MCP Config.
  2. Add the server under mcpServers (config below). Use a url for a remote/HTTP server (the ABAP Accelerator on :8000), or command + args for a local stdio server (community mcp-adt). Leave autoApprove empty so tool calls still surface for review.
  3. Save (Cmd+S / Ctrl+S). Kiro reconnects automatically — open the MCP Servers tab in the Kiro panel and confirm abap-accelerator shows Connected with its tools listed. (Trouble? Kiro panel → Output → Kiro - MCP Logs.)
// ~/.kiro/settings/mcp.json  —  ABAP Accelerator (HTTP server on :8000)
{
  "mcpServers": {
    "abap-accelerator": {
      "url": "http://localhost:8000/mcp",
      "disabled": false,
      "autoApprove": []
    }
  }
}

Keep autoApprove empty so write / table-content tools still surface for review (the Module 2 governance rule). Start the Accelerator first; Kiro then shows abap-accelerator as connected. The SAP credentials live with the server (securely, per Step 2) — not in mcp.json.

Alternative — community mcp-adt (stdio), if you installed it from source above:

// ~/.kiro/settings/mcp.json  —  community mcp-adt (stdio) alternative
{
  "mcpServers": {
    "sap-abap-adt": {
      "command": "python3",
      "args": ["/full/path/to/mcp-adt/mcp_server.py"],
      "timeout": 60
    }
  }
}

Verification

  • Open the chat panel in your IDE
  • Check the MCP tools icon — you should see sap-abap-adt listed as connected
  • If you see a red error, click "Fix Configuration" and check your path and .env file
Expected: MCP server shows as "Connected" with 15+ tools available

Setup Troubleshooting

If a step above did not work, find your symptom below before moving on:

Sign-in / authentication (Kiro):

  • Browser never opens: copy the sign-in URL shown in the IDE dialog and paste it into a browser manually.
  • "Code expired" or the tab hangs: the device code is short-lived. Cancel, start sign-in again, and complete it within a couple of minutes.
  • "Allow access" page loops back to sign-in: you are likely signed into a different AWS Builder ID in that browser. Open the consent page in a private window, or sign out of the other identity first.
  • Corporate proxy blocks the callback: set the IDE proxy (Kiro: Settings → search "proxy") and allow-list oidc.*.amazonaws.com and *.sso.*.amazonaws.com.

Chat panel not responding after sign-in:

  • Confirm the status bar shows a signed-in state (Kiro: an AWS profile). If not, sign out and back in.
  • Reload the IDE window (Command Palette → Developer: Reload Window) so the extension re-initializes.
  • Check your network can reach the model endpoint (a VPN or firewall may block it).

SAP system connection (optional lab):

  • Logon fails: re-check System ID, application server host, instance number, and client. Confirm the SAP user is not locked and the password is current.
  • Connection refused / timeout: ADT needs the SAP ICF/HTTP services active and network reachability (VPN) to the system.
  • Empty Project Explorer: your SAP user needs authorization for ADT/developer access; ask your Basis team to enable it.

Still stuck? Re-run just the failing step, and retry; the setup is designed to be quick to redo.

Still blocked after that? Reach out to your workshop facilitator or your organization's AWS/SAP support channel before moving on.

Congratulations! Your environment is ready. Next: Module 2 — Governed AI Development, where you turn Kiro’s steering and hooks into guardrails before any write to SAP.

Module 2: Governed AI Development

Before the hands-on modules, turn your setup into a governed setup. The same two mechanisms you met in Module 1 — steering files and agent hooks — are not just productivity features; used deliberately they are your guardrails. This short module wires them up so every lab that follows runs with the brakes on: unsafe writes are blocked, generated code must pass a quality gate, nothing reaches a transport without a human, security is generated in rather than bolted on, and business data stays out of the model.

The principle: an AI agent that can write to your SAP system is only as safe as the controls around it. “The agent usually does the right thing” is not a control. Make the right thing the only thing it can do.

Learning objectives

  • Block unsafe agent writes with a PreToolUse hook instead of trusting the prompt
  • Make a named ATC variant the mandatory quality gate for generated code
  • Keep generated objects in $TMP and route them to a transport only through human review
  • Generate secure CDS/RAP by default (DCL + authorization), including the Lab 8.1 endpoints
  • Capture behaviour with characterization tests before refactoring legacy code
  • Keep business data (table rows) out of the LLM and sign in with enterprise identity

Set these up in Kiro — step by step

This module relies on three Kiro constructs: a steering file (always-on project rules), an agent hook (deterministic enforcement around tool calls), and optionally a skill (an on-demand, packaged workflow). Create them once and every lab that follows runs governed. Steps below are for the Kiro IDE; the Kiro CLI uses the same files, you just create them on disk.

What are these, and why do they matter?

  • Steering file — a plain markdown file of standing instructions Kiro reads on every request (your conventions, tech stack, clean-core rules). Why: you stop re-explaining standards in each chat and every generation follows the same rules by default. It is guidance — a strong default the model follows almost all the time.
  • Agent hook — a small config that automatically runs your own code (or a prompt) when an event fires — for governance, before a tool call (PreToolUse). Why: a steering rule is a suggestion the agent usually honours; a hook is enforcement. It can veto an unsafe action (exit code 2), so “never activate without ATC” becomes something the agent cannot skip rather than something it is merely told.
  • Skill (optional) — a reusable, packaged workflow Kiro loads only when it is relevant (or when you invoke it with /). Why: keeps specialised know-how out of the way until you actually need it.

In short: a steering file shapes what the agent tends to do; a hook controls what it is allowed to do. Governance needs both — guidance and a guardrail.

A. Create a steering file (your clean-core rules)

Steering files are markdown that give Kiro persistent project knowledge. Workspace rules live in .kiro/steering/*.md; personal rules that apply to every project live in ~/.kiro/steering/ (workspace wins on conflict).

  1. Open the Kiro panel → Agent Steering & Skills.
  2. Click Generate to scaffold the foundation files (product.md, tech.md, structure.md), or + to add your own, e.g. abap.md.
  3. Write your rules in markdown (the clean-core + ATC-gate policy from §2 belongs here).
  4. Optionally set an inclusion mode in front-matter: always (default), fileMatch with a fileMatchPattern, or manual (loaded only when you reference it with #).
  5. Save. New chats pick it up automatically.
---
inclusion: always
---
# ABAP clean-core rules
- Consume RELEASED APIs and released CDS views only (check the API state)
- ATC variant Z_AI_GATE must pass (0 P1/P2, no pragma/pseudo-comment suppression) before activation
- Generate into $TMP; a human releases transports (never the agent)
- DCL + authorization by default on CDS/RAP; keep business data out of prompts

CLI: no UI needed — just create the file at .kiro/steering/abap.md.

B. Create an agent hook (the enforcement point)

Hooks run a shell command or an agent prompt automatically when an event fires. Hook configs are JSON files at .kiro/hooks/<id>.json. For governance you want PreToolUse, which can veto a tool call (exit code 2 blocks it and feeds the reason back to the agent).

  1. Easiest — ask Kiro in chat: “Create a PreToolUse hook that blocks the ABAP Accelerator release tool and gates activate on ATC variant Z_AI_GATE.” Kiro writes the hook file for you.
  2. Or create .kiro/hooks/abap-write-gate.json by hand with the v1 schema below.
  3. Add the gate script .kiro/hooks/abap_write_gate.sh and chmod +x it. The event (tool name + arguments) arrives as JSON on STDIN; the full script is in §1 below.
  4. The hook activates automatically — no prompting needed. Test it (try to activate before ATC → blocked).
{
  "version": "v1",
  "hooks": [
    {
      "name": "abap-write-gate",
      "trigger": "PreToolUse",
      "matcher": "abap-accelerator.*(create|update|activate|release)",
      "action": { "type": "command", "command": "./.kiro/hooks/abap_write_gate.sh" }
    }
  ]
}

C. (Optional) Package it as a skill

A skill is a portable instruction package (the open Agent Skills standard): a folder with a SKILL.md. Use a skill when you want an on-demand, reusable workflow rather than always-on rules (a steering file is always-on; a skill loads only when its description matches your request, or when you invoke it as a slash command). Workspace skills live in .kiro/skills/<name>/; personal ones in ~/.kiro/skills/.

  1. Create a folder .kiro/skills/abap-clean-core/ with a SKILL.md inside.
  2. Add front-matter with a name and a clear description — Kiro matches requests against the description to decide when to load the skill. Put the instructions in the body; add scripts/templates in the folder if needed.
  3. View and manage it in the Kiro panel → Agent Steering & Skills.
  4. Use it: Kiro auto-activates it when a request matches, or invoke it directly as a slash command /abap-clean-core.
---
name: abap-clean-core
description: Generate clean-core ABAP for this SAP project — released APIs only, DCL + authorization by default, ATC Z_AI_GATE must pass before activate, generate in $TMP and let a human release the transport.
---
# ABAP clean-core skill
When generating or changing ABAP in this project:
1. Use only RELEASED APIs and released CDS views.
2. Add DCL + authorization checks by default.
3. Generate into $TMP; never release a transport (a human does).
4. Run ATC variant Z_AI_GATE and fix P1/P2 before proposing activation.

1. Enforce, don’t suggest — block unsafe writes with a PreToolUse hook

Putting “never activate without ATC” in a steering file is a suggestion. The model follows suggestions most of the time. A hook is an enforcement point: it runs deterministic code around a tool call and can veto it.

Why not a file-save hook? On a normal project you’d hook “on file save”. But the ABAP Accelerator doesn’t save local files — it writes straight into SAP over ADT through its MCP tools. So the event you must gate is the MCP write tool call itself (create / update / activate / release), not a file save.

Add a PreToolUse hook that matches the Accelerator’s write tools and runs a gate script. A non-zero exit (exit code 2) blocks the tool call and feeds the reason back to the agent. (Schema below is the current Kiro hooks v1 format; see the Kiro hooks docs for the full trigger list.)

{
  "version": "v1",
  "hooks": [
    {
      "name": "abap-write-gate",
      "trigger": "PreToolUse",
      "matcher": "abap-accelerator.*(create|update|activate|release)",
      "action": { "type": "command", "command": "./.kiro/hooks/abap_write_gate.sh" }
    }
  ]
}

The gate script enforces policy in plain code — for example: refuse any release tool call outright (humans release transports, see §3), and refuse activate unless the ATC gate (§2) has just passed:

#!/usr/bin/env bash
# .kiro/hooks/abap_write_gate.sh  — exit 2 blocks the tool call
# Kiro passes the PreToolUse event (tool name + args) as JSON on STDIN.
event="$(cat)"
case "$event" in
  *release*)  echo "BLOCKED: the agent never releases transports — a human does."; exit 2 ;;
  *activate*) [ -f .kiro/state/atc_passed ] || { echo "BLOCKED: run ATC variant Z_AI_GATE (0 P1/P2) before activating."; exit 2 ; } ;;
esac
exit 0

Pair this with the SAP side: ATC runs again automatically on transport release, so even a mistaken activation can’t travel downstream unchecked.

Expected: when the agent tries to activate before ATC, or tries to release a transport, the tool call is refused and the agent is told why — without you watching.

2. The ATC quality gate (Z_AI_GATE)

Generated code is only trustworthy if it clears the same bar as hand-written code. Define a dedicated ATC check variant and make it mandatory.

# Add to .kiro/steering/abap.md

## Quality gate (ATC)
- After every generation and BEFORE any activation, run ATC with variant Z_AI_GATE.
- Z_AI_GATE must report ZERO priority-1 and priority-2 findings.
- NEVER silence a finding with a pragma (##NEEDED, ##NO_HANDLER, ...) or a
  pseudo-comment ("#EC ...). Fix the code instead.
- If priority-1/2 findings remain after 3 fix iterations, STOP and ask a human.

The Accelerator can run ATC and remediate for you — the point of the variant and the iteration cap is to make “clean” objective and to stop the agent looping forever or “fixing” findings by hiding them.

3. From $TMP to a transport — the review path

Let the agent create and iterate in the local object space ($TMP, non-transportable). Promotion to a transportable package is a human step:

  1. Agent generates & iterates in $TMP until ATC (Z_AI_GATE) is clean.
  2. A developer reviews the diff (via abapGit or gCTS) — not just the agent’s summary.
  3. On approval, the developer moves the objects into a transportable package and assigns the transport.
  4. Four-eyes: a second person releases the transport. The agent never releases (enforced by the hook in §1).
Describe, don’t release. Have the agent write a clear transport description of what changed and why — that becomes the reviewer’s starting point, and keeps a human in the loop at the one step that leaves the sandbox.

4. Secure coding, generated in

Security is cheapest when it’s part of the generation prompt and the steering rules — not a later audit. Add this to steering so every CDS/RAP artifact is born with access control:

# Add to .kiro/steering/abap.md

## Secure by default
- Every CDS view that exposes business data gets a DCL access control
  (@AccessControl.authorizationCheck: #CHECK) — no #NOT_REQUIRED on real data.
- Every RAP behavior and exposed service defines authorization (master/instance).
- REST/OData endpoints are authenticated AND authorization-checked — no anonymous endpoints.
- Validate and type all inputs; never build Open SQL from unchecked strings.

A matching DCL the agent should produce alongside a view like ZI_SalesOrderItem:

@EndUserText.label: 'Access control for ZI_SalesOrderItem'
@MappingRole: true
define role ZI_SalesOrderItem {
  grant select on ZI_SalesOrderItem
    where ( SalesOrganization ) = aspect pfcg_auth( V_VBAK_VKO, VKORG, ACTVT = '03' );
}

This is also the fix for the Lab 8.1 REST endpoints: bring their authentication and authorization into scope during the build, so the AI-DLC walkthrough ships a secured service, not an open one.

5. Characterization tests before you refactor

Before the Module 5 modernization labs (starting Lab 5.1), make the agent pin current behaviour first. Characterization (golden-master) tests catch the refactor that is clean and subtly wrong.

Before refactoring, write ABAP Unit tests that capture the CURRENT output of this
report for 3 representative inputs (characterization / golden-master tests).
Create the test class in $TMP only, and do NOT change the production code yet.
Then refactor until these characterization tests still pass.
Harness stays in $TMP. Any throwaway “fail-to-print” / live-comparison harness lives strictly in $TMP and is never promoted to a transport — it’s scaffolding, not a deliverable.

6. Keep business data out of the model

The Accelerator and read-only connectors (e.g. sap-odata) can return table rows. Those rows are business data — keep them out of the LLM unless you have a reason and consent.

  • Block table-content / SQL-result tools for the agent (don’t auto-approve them). Let it read structure and metadata (DDIC, released APIs, signatures) to generate code; it rarely needs the actual rows.
  • When a real example is needed, sanitize first — the same discipline as the dump in Lab 6.2 and the Securing credentials callout.
  • Sign in with enterprise identity (IAM Identity Center / your SSO) rather than personal accounts, so prompts and context stay inside your organization’s tenant and governance.

Governance checklist

  • PreToolUse hook blocks release and gates activate on ATC
  • Z_AI_GATE variant exists; 0 P1/P2; no pragma/pseudo-comment suppression
  • Generate in $TMP → diff review (abapGit/gCTS) → four-eyes release
  • Steering enforces DCL + authorization; Lab 8.1 endpoints secured
  • Characterization tests written before any Module 5 refactor
  • Table-content/SQL tools not auto-approved; enterprise sign-in in use
Expected: with these controls in place, every later lab runs inside guardrails — the agent can move fast because the dangerous moves are simply unavailable.

Module 3: ABAP Code Generation (45 minutes)

Learning Objectives

  • Generate ABAP code using natural language prompts
  • Use inline code suggestions for ABAP development
  • Understand how to write effective prompts for ABAP

Warm-Up Exercise (2 minutes)

Before we start the real labs, let's build confidence with a simple prompt. Copy and paste this into your chat:

Write a simple ABAP report that prints "Hello, Kiro!" to the screen. Use modern ABAP syntax.
Expected: You should get a short report with WRITE or cl_demo_output
If you get stuck: This is just a warm-up. If it doesn't work, check your connection in Module 1. You can skip ahead and come back.

3.1 Prompting Strategies for ABAP

Effective prompts for ABAP code generation should include:

  1. Context — SAP module (MM, SD, FI), system version (ECC, S/4HANA)
  2. Specifics — Table names, field names, transaction codes
  3. Standards — Clean ABAP, naming conventions, modern syntax
  4. Output format — Report, class, CDS view, function module

Good vs. Bad Prompts

Vague Prompt Specific Prompt
Write code to read purchase orders Write an ABAP report that reads purchase orders from EKKO/EKPO, filters by company code (BUKRS) and creation date (AEDAT) using selection screen parameters, and displays results in an ALV grid using CL_SALV_TABLE
Create a CDS view for sales Create a CDS view entity joining VBAK and VBAP with associations to I_BusinessPartner and I_Product, exposing sales order number, item, material, quantity, net value, and currency

Hands-On Lab 3.1: Generate an ALV Report (MM · Purchase Orders)

Instructions

  1. Open your Kiro chat panel
  2. Enter the following prompt:
Write an ABAP report that:
- Has a selection screen with parameters for company code (BUKRS) and
  a select-option for document date (AEDAT)
- Reads purchase order headers (EKKO) and items (EKPO) using a JOIN
- Displays results in an ALV grid using CL_SALV_TABLE
- Uses modern ABAP syntax (inline declarations, string templates)
- Follows Clean ABAP naming conventions

(ABAP Accelerator, if connected: then create and activate these objects in my SAP system, running syntax and ATC checks and iterating until clean.)

  2. Copy it into your ABAP project

Expected Output Structure

REPORT z_po_alv_report.

" Selection screen
PARAMETERS: p_bukrs TYPE bukrs OBLIGATORY.
SELECT-OPTIONS: s_aedat FOR sy-datum.

START-OF-SELECTION.

  " Data retrieval with JOIN
  SELECT e~ebeln, e~bukrs, e~aedat, e~lifnr,
         p~ebelp, p~matnr, p~menge, p~netpr
    FROM ekko AS e
    INNER JOIN ekpo AS p ON e~ebeln = p~ebeln
    WHERE e~bukrs = @p_bukrs
      AND e~aedat IN @s_aedat
    INTO TABLE @DATA(lt_po_data).

  " ALV display
  TRY.
      cl_salv_table=>factory(
        IMPORTING r_salv_table = DATA(lo_alv)
        CHANGING  t_table      = lt_po_data ).
      lo_alv->display( ).
    CATCH cx_salv_msg INTO DATA(lx_msg).
      MESSAGE lx_msg->get_text( ) TYPE 'E'.
  ENDTRY.
Expected: Kiro generates a complete report using CL_SALV_TABLE with a JOIN (no SELECT *) and a selection screen for company code and date; it activates with no syntax errors.

Hands-On Lab 3.4: Generate a Draw.io Architecture Diagram

Kiro can also generate draw.io XML that you can import directly into diagrams.net (draw.io) to visualize your ABAP architecture.

Instructions

Generate a draw.io file (.drawio XML format) and save it to [your-path]/sap-sales-order-flow.drawio. The diagram should show the architecture of a sales order flow with these components and numbered flow:

7. Kiro shown as a side panel with capabilities (code gen, explain, debug, modernize, test)

Include a color legend.

Color scheme:

- RAP/OData layer: #FF9900 (AWS orange)
- Database layer: #1B660F (green)
- External systems: #879596 (gray)
- Kiro panel: #232F3E background with #FF9900 accent

Use layer background rectangles, numbered arrows between components, and orthogonal edge routing. Output as a complete .drawio file I can open directly.

  2. Open it in app.diagrams.net (File → Open) or double-click the .drawio file

Hands-On Lab 3.6: ALV with Variant → Excel → Email / Share Drive

Real customer scenario: run an existing ALV report using a saved layout variant, export the result to Excel, and either email it to users or drop it on a share drive — as a scheduled background job.

Instructions

  1. Enter the following prompt in Kiro chat:
Generate an ABAP report that:
- Runs an existing ALV report program via SUBMIT ... USING SELECTION-SET '<VARIANT>'
  and captures its output
- Exports the result to a .xlsx file using whichever spreadsheet API is released and available in your S/4HANA release (for example the XCO spreadsheet APIs, cl_salv_export, or abap2xlsx) -- ask the assistant to detect and use what your system supports
- Sends the file as an email attachment via CL_BCS to a list of recipients
- OR writes the file to an application-server directory via OPEN DATASET (for a shared drive)
- Runs cleanly as a background job (no screen output); write results to the job log
Follow Clean ABAP: explicit field lists, no SELECT *, RETURNING params, exception handling.
Then run ATC via the ABAP Accelerator and remediate any findings.
  1. Review the generated report and job structure
  2. Verify it includes:
    • SUBMIT ... USING SELECTION-SET for the saved variant
    • XLSX generation via a released, available spreadsheet API
    • CL_BCS email send with attachment
    • OPEN DATASET path for the share-drive option
    • Background-job-safe (no WRITE to list)
  3. Ask the ABAP Accelerator to run ATC and activate the objects.
Expected: A background-job-ready report that runs the saved variant, produces an .xlsx, and either emails it via CL_BCS or writes it to a server directory — ATC-clean and activated.
Setup needed: a saved ALV variant for the source report; SAPconnect (SCOT) + an SMTP relay for CL_BCS email; for the share-drive option a logical file path (FILE) and an OS-mounted share on the SAP host; background-job authorization (SM36). No extra AWS services unless you host the relay (SES) or share (FSx/EFS/S3) on AWS.

Hands-On Lab 3.7: Normalize Multi-Format Excel Files

Real customer scenario: several source teams send the same data in Excel, each with a different column layout. Generate a program that reads them all and produces one canonical format.

Instructions

  1. Enter the following prompt in Kiro chat:
Generate an ABAP program that:
- Reads multiple source Excel (.xlsx) files that use DIFFERENT column layouts / headers
- Parses each workbook with whatever Excel-reading API is released and available in your release (the XCO spreadsheet APIs, abap2xlsx, or a custom reader)
- Maps each source layout to ONE canonical structure via a configurable
  field-mapping table (source header -> target field)
- Validates each row (mandatory fields, data types, value ranges); collects
  rejected rows into an error log with a reason
- Outputs a single normalized dataset (internal table / one canonical .xlsx)
Follow Clean ABAP: explicit types, no SELECT *, RETURNING params, exception handling.
Then run ATC via the ABAP Accelerator and remediate findings.
  1. Review the generated program
  2. Verify it includes:
    • A configurable source-header → target-field mapping (not hard-coded)
    • XLSX parsing via an available released API
    • Per-row validation with an error/reject log
    • One canonical output structure
    • Clean ABAP (explicit types, exception handling)
  3. Ask the ABAP Accelerator to run ATC and activate the objects.
Expected: A program that reads several differently-formatted .xlsx inputs, maps them via a configurable mapping table to one canonical structure, validates rows (rejects logged with reasons), and emits a single normalized dataset — ATC-clean.

Hands-On Lab 3.8: Generate a Status-Change Handler (event-driven)

Real customer scenario: run logic automatically when a transaction changes status — e.g., a Maintenance Notification moves from Open to In process.

Instructions

  1. Enter the following prompt in Kiro chat:
Generate ABAP for an event-driven status-change handler:
- React when a business object changes status (example: a Maintenance Notification
  moves from Open to In process)
- Use a released extension point: a BAdI implementation, a RAP determination/validation,
  or a status-management event handler -- no core modification
- On the status change, run the required action (create a follow-up, send a
  notification, update a Z-table via a released API)
- Make it idempotent and re-entrant; log outcomes; raise typed exceptions
- Clean core: released APIs only, no direct table writes
Then run ATC via the ABAP Accelerator and activate.
Note: wiring the SAP Business Workflow event linkage (transaction SWETYPV / event) is a
manual config step in SAP.
  1. Review the generated handler
  2. Verify it includes:
    • A released extension point (BAdI / RAP determination / status event) — no core mod
    • Triggered on the specific status transition
    • Idempotent / re-entrant with outcome logging
    • Released APIs only (no direct table writes)
  3. Ask the ABAP Accelerator to run ATC and activate. Then wire the Workflow event linkage in SAP.
Expected: An event-driven handler (BAdI / RAP determination / status event) that fires on the status change and runs the follow-up via released APIs — idempotent, logged, ATC-clean. The SAP Workflow event linkage is wired manually in SAP.
Setup needed: developer auth to create the BAdI / RAP determination / status handler; the target object’s status profile; SAP Business Workflow basic config (SWU3) and event linkage (SWETYPV) to actually trigger it; SAPconnect (SCOT) if it emails. Kiro generates the ABAP; the Workflow wiring is manual in SAP.
Capstone prompt — AnyCompany Fiori launchpad (live SAP data)

Code generation isn’t only ABAP. Hand Kiro this spec and it generates a complete client-side SAP Fiori launchpad for “AnyCompany” — UI5 views, controllers, and a live data snapshot — pulling real figures from S/4HANA through the sap-odata MCP (paged $top/$skip reads), with KPI tiles, List Report / Object Page drill-downs, and a hand-rendered P&L chart.

Show the capstone prompt (copy into Kiro) 
Build a client-side SAP Fiori Launchpad demo web app for "AnyCompany", styled with the
SAPUI5 Fiori Horizon theme (Quartz Light, SAP 72 font, semantic Good/Critical/Error colors).
Put it in a folder called fiori-launchpad/ (index.html, app.js, styles.css, live-data.json).
Load SAPUI5 from the OpenUI5 CDN (sdk.openui5.org), theme sap_horizon, libs
sap.m, sap.ui.core, sap.f, sap.ui.layout, sap.ui.unified ONLY -- do not reference
sap.ushell, sap.viz, or sap.suite.ui.microchart (they 404 on the public CDN and break boot).
Do not use sap.f.SearchManager.

DATA -- everything must come LIVE from SAP, nothing hardcoded. Use the SAP OData MCP tools
to pull the data. If a query is large, fetch it directly from the SAP OData endpoint in
paged batches (use $top + $skip, ~100 rows per page, add $select to keep payloads small)
rather than one big call, because large single responses crash the connection. Bake the
results into live-data.json as a snapshot with a fetchedAt timestamp, and have the app
read that snapshot at load so no tile is ever empty on launch.
Sources:
  - Total Materials:      API_PRODUCT_SRV / A_Product, ProductType eq 'FERT' (count)
  - Low Stock Items:      API_MATERIAL_STOCK_SRV / A_MatlStkInAcctMod, Plant 1710
                          (count where on-hand qty < reorder point; on-hand is live, and
                          since the sandbox has no reorder field, synthesize a deterministic
                          per-material reorder point and label it as demo-derived in the
                          snapshot meta -- do not pass it off as a live field)
  - Open Purchase Orders: API_PURCHASEORDER_PROCESS_SRV / A_PurchaseOrder, CompanyCode 1710,
                          open = PurchasingProcessingStatus 02 or 03
  - Sales Orders + Value: API_SALES_ORDER_SRV / A_SalesOrder, SalesOrganization 1710
                          (count + sum of TotalNetAmount)
  - Revenue/Expenses/P&L: API_JOURNALENTRYITEMBASIC_SRV / A_JournalEntryItemBasic,
                          CompanyCode 1710, Ledger 0L, LedgerFiscalYear 2025,
                          GLAccount 40000000-89999999 (note: field is LedgerFiscalYear,
                          GLAccount is an unpadded 8-digit string; revenue = GL 4xxxxxxx,
                          expenses = GL 5-8xxxxxxx; revenue posts as negative/credit).
                          Aggregate revenue, expenses, and a by-fiscal-period breakdown.

SHELL + CO-BRAND:
  - A thin co-brand strip at the very top (deep navy): the official SAP logo, the word "on",
    the official AWS logo (download both as public-domain SVGs into fiori-launchpad/assets/
    and reference them as local <img>; put the AWS logo on a white rounded chip since its
    wordmark is dark), and a "RISE with SAP" pill on the right.
  - Below it, an SAP Fiori shell bar (sap.f.ShellBar) titled "AnyCompany" with a search
    field, notification bell, and user avatar (initials "AM"). No "S/4HANA on RISE" text.

HOME -- a single launchpad page with a welcome hero header and tiles grouped into three
business "apps":
  - Sales (Order-to-cash): Sales Orders, Order Value
  - Finance (Record-to-report): Revenue FY2025, Profit & Loss (navigation tile)
  - Operations (Materials & procurement): Total Materials, Low Stock Items, Open Purchase Orders
  Each KPI tile shows a live number with its unit and a small footer naming the SAP business
  area (e.g. "Sales & Distribution", "Financial Accounting", "Material Master",
  "Inventory Management", "Procurement") with a green "live" status dot -- do NOT show raw
  OData service names. Color the Low Stock tile red when items are below reorder. If any
  dataset isn't available yet, show "-" with an "awaiting SAP" badge instead of a fake number.
  A snapshot footer shows host, client, and the fetched timestamp.

DRILL-DOWN:
  - Clicking a KPI tile opens a Fiori List Report page: a filter bar with live search and a
    responsive table (demand-popin columns), row count, and semantic status cells.
  - Clicking a row opens a Fiori Object Page with grouped detail sections.
  - Provide List Report + Object Page for Materials, Sales Orders, Open Purchase Orders, and
    Low Stock.

P&L ANALYTICAL PAGE (opens from the Revenue or Profit & Loss tile):
  - A KPI header with Revenue, Expenses, and Net Profit (with margin %), Net Profit card
    tinted green when positive / red when negative.
  - A "Revenue vs Expenses -- FY2025 by period" grouped bar chart built from the live
    by-period data (hand-rendered with HTML/CSS, no chart library), with gridlines, period
    labels, and a legend. Draw the chart only after its container is attached to the DOM
    (retry on animation frames), and guarantee the bars become visible even if the grow-in
    animation frame is missed.

POLISH (make it genuinely Fiori-grade, Operate mode):
  - Horizon design tokens, a clear type scale, tabular numerals for figures, tight-group /
    generous-separation spacing.
  - Theme the browser surfaces too: custom scrollbars, text selection, and focus rings from
    the palette.
  - One restrained motion moment (hero rise, chart grow-in using transform not height/width),
    honoring prefers-reduced-motion.
  - A subtle premium background behind the launchpad (brand-tinted radial wash + faint fading
    grid mesh), kept quiet so tiles stay the focus.
  - Full hover/focus/active/empty/error/loading states, and a single-column phone layout /
    two-up tablet / auto-fill desktop grid with no horizontal overflow.
  - No AI-tell anti-patterns: no thick colored side-border on cards, no emoji standing in for
    icons (draw icons as SVG), no gradient text.
  - Add ?v=<n> cache-busting query strings on app.js and styles.css.

Serve the folder over HTTP (e.g. python3 -m http.server 4173) -- not file:// -- because the
app fetches live-data.json. Verify the final result renders correctly on desktop and mobile
with no console errors before finishing.

Module 4: ABAP Code Explanation & Documentation (30 minutes)

Learning Objectives

  • Use Kiro to explain legacy ABAP code
  • Generate documentation for existing programs

4.1 Why Code Explanation Matters

SAP systems often contain decades of custom ABAP code with:

  • Minimal or outdated documentation
  • Complex business logic embedded in nested loops
  • Dynamic programming (field symbols, ASSIGN, GENERATE SUBROUTINE POOL)
  • Implicit dependencies on SAP standard behavior

Kiro can analyze ABAP code and explain the business logic, data flow, and potential issues.

Hands-On Lab 4.1: Explain Legacy Code

Instructions

  1. Copy the following legacy ABAP code into your editor or your Kiro chat:
REPORT z_legacy_sales_report.

TABLES: vbak, vbap, kna1.

DATA: lt_vbak TYPE TABLE OF vbak,
      ls_vbak TYPE vbak,
      lt_vbap TYPE TABLE OF vbap,
      ls_vbap TYPE vbap,
      lv_total TYPE vbap-netwr,
      lv_count TYPE i,
      lt_kna1 TYPE HASHED TABLE OF kna1 WITH UNIQUE KEY kunnr.

SELECT-OPTIONS: s_erdat FOR vbak-erdat,
                s_vkorg FOR vbak-vkorg.

START-OF-SELECTION.

SELECT * FROM vbak INTO TABLE lt_vbak
  WHERE erdat IN s_erdat
    AND vkorg IN s_vkorg
    AND vbtyp = 'C'.

IF lt_vbak IS NOT INITIAL.
  SELECT * FROM kna1 INTO TABLE lt_kna1
    FOR ALL ENTRIES IN lt_vbak
    WHERE kunnr = lt_vbak-kunnr.
ENDIF.

LOOP AT lt_vbak INTO ls_vbak.
  SELECT * FROM vbap INTO TABLE lt_vbap
    WHERE vbeln = ls_vbak-vbeln.
  CLEAR lv_total.
  LOOP AT lt_vbap INTO ls_vbap.
    lv_total = lv_total + ls_vbap-netwr.
    lv_count = lv_count + 1.
  ENDLOOP.
  READ TABLE lt_kna1 INTO DATA(ls_kna1)
    WITH TABLE KEY kunnr = ls_vbak-kunnr.
  WRITE: / ls_vbak-vbeln, ls_vbak-erdat, ls_kna1-name1, lv_total, lv_count.
  CLEAR lv_count.
ENDLOOP.
  1. Ask Kiro:
Explain this ABAP code in detail. Describe:
1. The business purpose
2. The data flow
3. Any performance issues
4. Suggestions for improvement
  1. Review the explanation and verify Kiro identifies:
    • The report reads sales orders (VBTYP = 'C') filtered by date and sales org
    • It performs a nested SELECT inside a LOOP (N+1 query problem)
    • Customer names are fetched using a hashed table (good pattern)
    • The WRITE statement outputs a flat list
    • Performance issue: SELECT inside LOOP for VBAP
Expected: Kiro returns a structured explanation covering business purpose, data flow, performance issues, and improvement suggestions — matching the requested outline.

Hands-On Lab 4.2: Generate Technical Documentation

Instructions

  1. Use the same code from Lab 4.1 and prompt:
Generate technical documentation for this ABAP report in the following format:
- Program Name & Description
- Selection Screen Parameters
- Database Tables Used
- Processing Logic (step by step)
- Output Description
- Known Limitations
- Dependencies
  1. Review the generated documentation for accuracy and completeness.
Expected: Documentation covering program name, selection parameters, tables used, step-by-step logic, and output, in the requested format.

Hands-On Lab 4.3: Explain Dynamic ABAP Code

  1. Ask Kiro to explain this dynamic programming pattern:
FIELD-SYMBOLS: <lt_table> TYPE STANDARD TABLE,
               <ls_line>  TYPE any,
               <lv_field> TYPE any.

DATA: lo_descr  TYPE REF TO cl_abap_structdescr,
      lt_comp   TYPE abap_compdescr_tab,
      lr_data   TYPE REF TO data.

lo_descr ?= cl_abap_typedescr=>describe_by_name( iv_table_name ).
lt_comp = lo_descr->components.

CREATE DATA lr_data TYPE TABLE OF (iv_table_name).
ASSIGN lr_data->* TO <lt_table>.

SELECT * FROM (iv_table_name) INTO TABLE <lt_table> UP TO 100 ROWS.

LOOP AT <lt_table> ASSIGNING <ls_line>.
  LOOP AT lt_comp INTO DATA(ls_comp).
    ASSIGN COMPONENT ls_comp-name OF STRUCTURE <ls_line> TO <lv_field>.
    WRITE: / ls_comp-name, ':', <lv_field>.
  ENDLOOP.
ENDLOOP.
  1. Prompt:
Explain this dynamic ABAP code. What does it do, and what are the
security implications of using dynamic table names?
Expected: Kiro explains the dynamic constructs (field-symbols, PERFORM, dynamic SELECT) and flags the maintainability and security implications.

Checkpoint

  • Successfully explained legacy ABAP code
  • Generated technical documentation
  • Understand how Kiro handles dynamic ABAP patterns

Hands-On Lab 4.4: Validate a Program Against its Functional Spec

Real customer scenario: you have a Functional Specification (FS) and the ABAP program a developer wrote from it. Use Kiro to check whether the program actually implements the spec — clause by clause — and flag gaps, deviations, and missing edge cases.

Instructions

  1. Open the ABAP program (or paste the source), attach or paste the Functional Spec, then enter:
Compare this ABAP program against the attached Functional Spec. Produce a compliance report:
1. A clause-by-clause table: each FS requirement -> Implemented / Partial / Missing -> evidence (method or line)
2. Deviations: where the code does something the spec did not ask for, or differs from it
3. Missing edge cases / validations the spec implies but the code omits
4. Clean-core / released-API concerns
5. A short prioritized list of changes to bring the program in line with the spec
Do not change the code yet -- just report.
  1. Review the compliance table
  2. Verify Kiro:
    • Maps every FS clause to Implemented / Partial / Missing
    • Cites evidence (method / line) for each
    • Flags deviations and missing validations
    • Gives a prioritized remediation list
  3. Optional: follow up with “apply the Priority-1 fixes” and let the ABAP Accelerator ATC-check the result.
Expected: A clause-by-clause compliance table (Implemented / Partial / Missing) with evidence, a deviations list, missing-validation callouts, and a prioritized remediation plan — no code changed yet.

Tie-in: this is the reverse of AI-DLC’s Inception (Module 8) — instead of spec → code, you go code → spec-compliance. Same principle: the Functional Spec is the source of truth.

Module 5: Clean Core Modernization & Refactoring (45 minutes)

Learning Objectives

  • Understand SAP's clean core strategy and its six dimensions
  • Modernize legacy ABAP toward clean core: Clean ABAP, released APIs, and ABAP Cloud
  • Refactor classical patterns to modern, upgrade-stable equivalents

5.0 The Clean Core Strategy

Clean core is SAP's framework of best practices for keeping SAP S/4HANA (Cloud Private or Public Edition) and its extensions upgrade-stable and cloud-compliant. The core principle: extend SAP to meet your unique requirements without modifying the core application. A clean core improves performance across six dimensions:

Dimension What "clean" means Where Kiro helps
Software stack Stay close to standard; no modifications to SAP objects Refactor mods into released extension points
Extensibility Use released APIs, ABAP Cloud/RAP (on-stack) or BTP/CAP (side-by-side) Generate RAP/CAP artifacts and released-API code
Integrations API-led, event-driven, standard integration scenarios Generate OData/REST integration code
Data Clean, high-quality master data; archiving Explain data flows, spot quality issues
Processes Standard processes, minimal custom logic Assess and simplify custom code
Operations Streamlined, monitorable, low-risk operations Analyze dumps, optimize performance

Why it matters: Heavy core customization makes upgrades slow, risky, and expensive. Clean core keeps you current with new SAP features at lower cost. This module focuses on the software stack and extensibility dimensions: the code-level work of getting clean.

5.1 Modernization Targets

Legacy Pattern Modern Replacement
DATA: lv_var TYPE ... DATA(lv_var) = ... (inline declaration)
CONCATENATE a b INTO c c = \|{ a }{ b }\| (string templates)
CREATE OBJECT lo_obj lo_obj = NEW #( )
CALL METHOD lo_obj->method lo_obj->method( )
MOVE a TO b b = a
SELECT * FROM ... SELECT field1, field2 FROM ...
REUSE_ALV_GRID_DISPLAY CL_SALV_TABLE
READ TABLE ... WITH KEY READ TABLE ... WITH TABLE KEY or line_exists( )
Header lines Explicit work areas
FORM/PERFORM Methods in classes

5.2 Clean ABAP Principles

  • Use meaningful, descriptive names — and apply them consistently. This workshop keeps the lightweight lv_/lt_/ls_/lo_ local prefixes defined in the .kiro/steering/abap.md steering file (see the naming-conventions table in Module 1). Clean ABAP itself leans away from encoded prefixes, so the rule that matters is: pick one scheme in your steering file and have Kiro follow it everywhere — don't mix.
  • Keep methods small and focused
  • Prefer functional over procedural style
  • Use exceptions instead of return codes
  • Avoid deep nesting

Hands-On Lab 5.1: Modernize the Legacy Report

Instructions

  1. Take the legacy code from Module 4, Lab 4.1
  2. Ask Kiro:
Refactor this ABAP report to follow Clean ABAP guidelines and modern syntax:
- Use inline declarations
- Replace SELECT * with explicit field lists
- Fix the N+1 SELECT problem (SELECT inside LOOP)
- Use string templates instead of WRITE
- Replace the flat list output with CL_SALV_TABLE
- Use modern ABAP syntax (NEW, VALUE, CORRESPONDING, etc.)
- Add proper error handling with TRY/CATCH
  1. Compare the before and after versions
  2. Verify the refactored code addresses:
    • No more SELECT *
    • No SELECT inside LOOP — uses JOIN or FOR ALL ENTRIES
    • Inline declarations used throughout
    • ALV output via CL_SALV_TABLE
    • Proper exception handling

Expected Transformation

Before: ~40 lines, 3 separate SELECTs (one inside a loop), WRITE output After: ~30 lines, single JOIN query, CL_SALV_TABLE output, inline declarations

Expected: The rewrite replaces SELECT * with explicit fields, removes any SELECT inside a LOOP, and uses modern syntax while preserving behavior.

Hands-On Lab 5.2: Convert to Clean Core Compatible Code (ABAP Cloud)

Instructions

  1. Prompt Kiro:
Rewrite this ABAP code to be clean core compliant and compatible with
ABAP Cloud (Tier 1 - released APIs only). Extend without modifying the
core. Replace any unreleased APIs with their released equivalents. The
code should work in SAP BTP ABAP Environment.

Specifically:
- Replace direct database table access with released CDS view consumption
- Use released APIs only (no access to non-released SAP objects)
- Follow the ABAP Cloud development model

(ABAP Accelerator, if connected: create/update and activate the changed objects in my SAP system, running ATC with my check variant and iterating until clean.)
  1. Review what changes Kiro suggests:
    • Direct table access → CDS view consumption
    • Unreleased classes → Released API equivalents
    • Classical output → RAP or OData-based approach
Expected: Code that compiles in ABAP Cloud (Tier 1) using only released APIs, with any unreleased calls replaced by released equivalents.

Hands-On Lab 5.3: Convert Subroutines to OO

  1. Provide code with FORM/PERFORM routines:
FORM calculate_tax USING iv_amount TYPE netwr
                         iv_country TYPE land1
                   CHANGING cv_tax TYPE netwr.
  CASE iv_country.
    WHEN 'DE'. cv_tax = iv_amount * '0.19'.
    WHEN 'US'. cv_tax = iv_amount * '0.08'.
    WHEN 'JP'. cv_tax = iv_amount * '0.10'.
    WHEN OTHERS. cv_tax = iv_amount * '0.15'.
  ENDCASE.
ENDFORM.

FORM get_customer_name USING iv_kunnr TYPE kunnr
                       CHANGING cv_name TYPE name1_gp.
  SELECT SINGLE name1 FROM kna1 INTO cv_name
    WHERE kunnr = iv_kunnr.
ENDFORM.
  1. Prompt:
Convert these FORM routines into a proper ABAP OO class with methods.
Follow Clean ABAP guidelines, use RETURNING parameters where possible,
and add appropriate exception handling.
Expected: A ZCL_ class whose methods replace the FORM routines, using RETURNING parameters where possible and proper exception handling per Clean ABAP.

Checkpoint

  • Modernized legacy code to Clean ABAP
  • Converted code to ABAP Cloud compatible
  • Refactored FORM routines to OO methods

Hands-On Lab 5.4: Migrate an Excel VBA Macro from ECC 6.0 to S/4 (OData)

Real customer scenario: an Excel macro talks to SAP ECC 6.0; migrate it to work against S/4HANA over Fiori/OData. This is a two-sided job — a released service on SAP, and a rewritten macro on the client.

Instructions

  1. Enter the following prompt in Kiro chat:
Help me migrate an Excel VBA macro from SAP ECC 6.0 to SAP S/4HANA. Two parts:
SAP side (via ABAP Accelerator):
- Expose the data/logic the macro needs as a released OData service using RAP
  (CDS view entity + service definition + service binding), clean-core compliant
- Give me the service URL and entity / field names
Client side (Excel/VBA):
- Rewrite the VBA macro to call the OData service over HTTPS (WinHTTP / MSXML),
  handle auth, parse the JSON response, and write results back to the sheet
- Replace the old ECC connection (SAP GUI Scripting / RFC / classic DI) with OData calls
- Keep the macro's user-facing behavior identical
Then run ATC on the ABAP side via the ABAP Accelerator and activate.
  1. Review both sides of the migration
  2. Verify it includes:
    • A released OData (RAP) service: CDS entity + service definition + binding
    • Clean-core compliant (released APIs, no core mod)
    • VBA rewritten to call OData over HTTPS + JSON parsing
    • Old ECC connection fully replaced
    • Same user-facing behavior preserved
  3. Ask the ABAP Accelerator to run ATC and activate the S/4 service.
Expected: A released OData (RAP) service on S/4 (CDS + service definition + binding, ATC-clean) plus a rewritten VBA macro that calls it over HTTPS and parses JSON — replacing the old ECC connection while preserving behavior.
Setup needed: two-sided. SAP: activate the OData service in SICF and configure auth (OAuth2/basic); if S/4 is on AWS, ensure the endpoint is reachable from the client network (VPN/Direct Connect, or public via ALB + WAF — security review). Client: Excel with HTTPS access, credentials/token, and TLS trust. The VBA rewrite is client work (Kiro general IDE), not the Accelerator.

Two-sided scope: the ABAP Accelerator builds and activates the S/4 OData service; the VBA rewrite is authored by Kiro as a general AI IDE — the Accelerator itself only touches ABAP objects.

Capstone prompt — AnyCompany Fiori launchpad (live SAP data)

Clean core isn’t only backend ABAP — it extends to how you surface data. Hand Kiro this spec to generate a client-side SAP Fiori launchpad for “AnyCompany” that consumes released OData services read-only through the sap-odata MCP (paged $top/$skip reads baked into a snapshot) — KPI tiles, List Report / Object Page drill-downs, and a hand-rendered P&L chart, all without touching the digital core.

Show the capstone prompt (copy into Kiro) 
Build a client-side SAP Fiori Launchpad demo web app for "AnyCompany", styled with the
SAPUI5 Fiori Horizon theme (Quartz Light, SAP 72 font, semantic Good/Critical/Error colors).
Put it in a folder called fiori-launchpad/ (index.html, app.js, styles.css, live-data.json).
Load SAPUI5 from the OpenUI5 CDN (sdk.openui5.org), theme sap_horizon, libs
sap.m, sap.ui.core, sap.f, sap.ui.layout, sap.ui.unified ONLY -- do not reference
sap.ushell, sap.viz, or sap.suite.ui.microchart (they 404 on the public CDN and break boot).
Do not use sap.f.SearchManager.

DATA -- everything must come LIVE from SAP, nothing hardcoded. Use the SAP OData MCP tools
to pull the data. If a query is large, fetch it directly from the SAP OData endpoint in
paged batches (use $top + $skip, ~100 rows per page, add $select to keep payloads small)
rather than one big call, because large single responses crash the connection. Bake the
results into live-data.json as a snapshot with a fetchedAt timestamp, and have the app
read that snapshot at load so no tile is ever empty on launch.
Sources:
  - Total Materials:      API_PRODUCT_SRV / A_Product, ProductType eq 'FERT' (count)
  - Low Stock Items:      API_MATERIAL_STOCK_SRV / A_MatlStkInAcctMod, Plant 1710
                          (count where on-hand qty < reorder point; on-hand is live, and
                          since the sandbox has no reorder field, synthesize a deterministic
                          per-material reorder point and label it as demo-derived in the
                          snapshot meta -- do not pass it off as a live field)
  - Open Purchase Orders: API_PURCHASEORDER_PROCESS_SRV / A_PurchaseOrder, CompanyCode 1710,
                          open = PurchasingProcessingStatus 02 or 03
  - Sales Orders + Value: API_SALES_ORDER_SRV / A_SalesOrder, SalesOrganization 1710
                          (count + sum of TotalNetAmount)
  - Revenue/Expenses/P&L: API_JOURNALENTRYITEMBASIC_SRV / A_JournalEntryItemBasic,
                          CompanyCode 1710, Ledger 0L, LedgerFiscalYear 2025,
                          GLAccount 40000000-89999999 (note: field is LedgerFiscalYear,
                          GLAccount is an unpadded 8-digit string; revenue = GL 4xxxxxxx,
                          expenses = GL 5-8xxxxxxx; revenue posts as negative/credit).
                          Aggregate revenue, expenses, and a by-fiscal-period breakdown.

SHELL + CO-BRAND:
  - A thin co-brand strip at the very top (deep navy): the official SAP logo, the word "on",
    the official AWS logo (download both as public-domain SVGs into fiori-launchpad/assets/
    and reference them as local <img>; put the AWS logo on a white rounded chip since its
    wordmark is dark), and a "RISE with SAP" pill on the right.
  - Below it, an SAP Fiori shell bar (sap.f.ShellBar) titled "AnyCompany" with a search
    field, notification bell, and user avatar (initials "AM"). No "S/4HANA on RISE" text.

HOME -- a single launchpad page with a welcome hero header and tiles grouped into three
business "apps":
  - Sales (Order-to-cash): Sales Orders, Order Value
  - Finance (Record-to-report): Revenue FY2025, Profit & Loss (navigation tile)
  - Operations (Materials & procurement): Total Materials, Low Stock Items, Open Purchase Orders
  Each KPI tile shows a live number with its unit and a small footer naming the SAP business
  area (e.g. "Sales & Distribution", "Financial Accounting", "Material Master",
  "Inventory Management", "Procurement") with a green "live" status dot -- do NOT show raw
  OData service names. Color the Low Stock tile red when items are below reorder. If any
  dataset isn't available yet, show "-" with an "awaiting SAP" badge instead of a fake number.
  A snapshot footer shows host, client, and the fetched timestamp.

DRILL-DOWN:
  - Clicking a KPI tile opens a Fiori List Report page: a filter bar with live search and a
    responsive table (demand-popin columns), row count, and semantic status cells.
  - Clicking a row opens a Fiori Object Page with grouped detail sections.
  - Provide List Report + Object Page for Materials, Sales Orders, Open Purchase Orders, and
    Low Stock.

P&L ANALYTICAL PAGE (opens from the Revenue or Profit & Loss tile):

    tinted green when positive / red when negative.

POLISH (make it genuinely Fiori-grade, Operate mode):
  - Horizon design tokens, a clear type scale, tabular numerals for figures, tight-group /
    generous-separation spacing.
  - Theme the browser surfaces too: custom scrollbars, text selection, and focus rings from
    the palette.
  - One restrained motion moment (hero rise, chart grow-in using transform not height/width),
    honoring prefers-reduced-motion.
  - A subtle premium background behind the launchpad (brand-tinted radial wash + faint fading
    grid mesh), kept quiet so tiles stay the focus.
  - Full hover/focus/active/empty/error/loading states, and a single-column phone layout /
    two-up tablet / auto-fill desktop grid with no horizontal overflow.
  - No AI-tell anti-patterns: no thick colored side-border on cards, no emoji standing in for
    icons (draw icons as SVG), no gradient text.
  - Add ?v=<n> cache-busting query strings on app.js and styles.css.

Module 6: Debugging & Troubleshooting ABAP (30 minutes)

Learning Objectives

  • Use Kiro to identify and fix ABAP runtime errors
  • Troubleshoot common SAP issues
  • Optimize ABAP performance

6.1 Common ABAP Issues Kiro Can Help With

Issue Type Examples
Runtime errors GETWA_NOT_ASSIGNED, ITAB_DUPLICATE_KEY, COMPUTE_INT_ZERODIVIDE
Performance SELECT in LOOP, missing indexes, large internal tables
Type mismatches Incompatible types in assignments, conversions
Logic errors Incorrect loop processing, missing CLEAR statements
Authorization Missing authority checks, SY-SUBRC handling

Hands-On Lab 6.1: Fix a Buggy Program

Instructions

  1. Review this ABAP program that contains multiple issues:
REPORT z_buggy_program.

DATA: lt_items TYPE TABLE OF vbap,
      lt_materials TYPE TABLE OF mara,
      lv_total TYPE p DECIMALS 2.

" Issue 1: SELECT * without WHERE - reads entire table
SELECT * FROM vbap INTO TABLE lt_items.

" Issue 2: SELECT inside LOOP (N+1 problem)
LOOP AT lt_items INTO DATA(ls_item).
  SELECT SINGLE * FROM mara INTO @DATA(ls_mara)
    WHERE matnr = @ls_item-matnr.

  " Issue 3: No SY-SUBRC check after SELECT SINGLE
  lv_total = lv_total + ls_item-netwr * ls_mara-ntgew.

  " Issue 4: READ TABLE without TRANSPORTING NO FIELDS for existence check
  READ TABLE lt_items INTO DATA(ls_check)
    WITH KEY vbeln = ls_item-vbeln
             posnr = ls_item-posnr.
ENDLOOP.

" Issue 5: Division without zero check
DATA(lv_avg) = lv_total / lines( lt_items ).

WRITE: / 'Average:', lv_avg.
  1. Ask Kiro:
This ABAP program has multiple bugs and performance issues.
Identify all issues and provide a corrected version.
  1. Verify Kiro identifies all 5 issues:
    • SELECT * without WHERE clause
    • SELECT inside LOOP
    • Missing SY-SUBRC check
    • Inefficient READ TABLE
    • Division by zero risk
Expected: Kiro lists each bug and performance issue and returns a corrected version that addresses all of them.

Hands-On Lab 6.2: Analyze an ABAP Dump

Instructions

  1. Simulate an ST22 dump analysis by providing this error context to Kiro:
I got this ABAP runtime error (sanitized sample from a production system):

Runtime Error: GETWA_NOT_ASSIGNED
Program: Z_PROCESS_ORDERS
Include: Z_PROCESS_ORDERS
Line: 42

Source code extract:
  FIELD-SYMBOLS: <ls_order> TYPE ty_order.
  READ TABLE lt_orders ASSIGNING <ls_order>
    WITH KEY order_id = lv_order_id.
  <ls_order>-status = 'COMPLETED'.    " <-- Line 42

The error occurs intermittently, only for certain order IDs.
What is the cause and how do I fix it?

Sanitize before you share. This dump is a fabricated teaching example — no real users, system IDs, clients, or document numbers. When analyzing a real ST22 dump with an AI, strip the identifying context first: system ID and client, user name, and any business data in the variable/parameter values (customer, material, order numbers, amounts). The call stack, error code, and source extract are what the model actually needs. Treat this as part of the same data-boundary discipline covered in the Governed AI Development module and the Securing credentials callout.

  1. Verify Kiro explains:
    • The field symbol is not assigned because READ TABLE didn't find a match
    • SY-SUBRC check is missing after READ TABLE
    • The fix: add IF sy-subrc = 0 or IF <ls_order> IS ASSIGNED
Expected: Kiro identifies the root cause (e.g., an unassigned field-symbol) and shows the guard/fix that prevents the dump.

Hands-On Lab 6.3: Performance Optimization

Instructions

  1. Provide this slow-performing code:
" This report takes 30+ minutes to run in production
LOOP AT lt_sales_orders INTO DATA(ls_so).
  LOOP AT lt_deliveries INTO DATA(ls_del)
    WHERE vbeln = ls_so-vbeln.
    LOOP AT lt_billing INTO DATA(ls_bill)
      WHERE vbeln = ls_del-vbeln.
      SELECT SINGLE * FROM bsad INTO @DATA(ls_cleared)
        WHERE bukrs = @ls_bill-bukrs
          AND belnr = @ls_bill-belnr.
      IF sy-subrc = 0.
        APPEND VALUE #(
          vbeln = ls_so-vbeln
          del_no = ls_del-vbeln
          bill_no = ls_bill-vbeln
          cleared = abap_true
        ) TO lt_result.
      ENDIF.
    ENDLOOP.
  ENDLOOP.
ENDLOOP.
  1. Prompt:
This ABAP code takes 30+ minutes in production. Analyze the performance
issues and rewrite it to run efficiently. Explain each optimization.
  1. Expected optimizations Kiro should suggest:
    • Replace nested LOOPs with sorted/hashed tables or secondary keys
    • Move SELECT out of the loop — use FOR ALL ENTRIES or JOIN
    • Consider using a single JOIN query to replace the entire nested structure
    • Use PARALLEL CURSOR technique if nested LOOPs are necessary
Expected: Kiro pinpoints the bottlenecks (e.g., nested SELECTs) and rewrites them with JOIN / FOR ALL ENTRIES, noting the expected gain.

Checkpoint

  • Identified and fixed multiple bugs in ABAP code
  • Analyzed a simulated ABAP dump
  • Optimized a slow-performing ABAP program

Module 7: Real-World Use Cases (30 minutes)

Learning Objectives

  • Apply Kiro to real SAP project scenarios

7.1 Use Case: S/4HANA Migration Preparation

Scenario

Your organization is migrating from ECC 6.0 to S/4HANA. You have 500+ custom ABAP programs that need compatibility assessment.

Lab Exercise

  1. Provide code that uses deprecated APIs:
" Uses direct BSEG access (not recommended in S/4HANA)
SELECT * FROM bseg INTO TABLE @DATA(lt_bseg)
  WHERE bukrs = @p_bukrs
    AND belnr = @p_belnr
    AND gjahr = @p_gjahr.

" Uses KONV direct access (replaced in S/4HANA)
SELECT * FROM konv INTO TABLE @DATA(lt_konv)
  WHERE knumv = @lv_knumv.

" Uses obsolete BDC approach
CALL TRANSACTION 'VA01' USING lt_bdcdata MODE 'N'.
  1. Prompt:
This ABAP code needs to be migrated to S/4HANA. Identify all
incompatible or deprecated patterns and provide S/4HANA-compatible
replacements. Reference the SAP simplification list where applicable.

(ABAP Accelerator, if connected: create/update and activate the changed objects in my SAP system, running ATC with my check variant and iterating until clean.)

7.5 Beyond Development: Kiro-CLI for SAP Operations

The same agentic AI approach extends past writing ABAP into running and troubleshooting SAP on AWS. An Aug 2026 AWS post shows how Kiro-CLI paired with the managed AWS MCP Server cuts SAP network troubleshooting from the typical 2–4 hours down to minutes — using plain-English prompts instead of memorizing VPC Flow Log, security group, and route table commands.

Note: This is an ops / Basis use case rather than an ABAP development one — it's included so developers know the same Kiro + MCP pattern they learned here applies to operations too. It's a "good to know," not a hands-on lab in this workshop.

How it works: Kiro-CLI is the natural-language interface; the MCP Server is the "hands" that call AWS APIs on your behalf through a single audited endpoint. You ask a question, it selects the right tools, runs the queries, and returns a correlated answer in plain English — keeping context for follow-ups. Setup is a one-time ~30–60 minute exercise (install Kiro-CLI → register the MCP Server → run a read-only prompt like "list my VPCs" to confirm access).

Example prompts

"Show me all rejected network traffic for my SAP application server in the last 12 hours, and tell me which security group rule is blocking it."

"Perform a comprehensive network health check for our SAP S/4HANA system. Analyze VPC Flow Logs, security groups, and performance metrics, and generate a health report with an executive summary."

This matters most for RISE with SAP landscapes, where connectivity crosses AWS account boundaries and manual diagnosis is slowest.

Kiro-CLI — SAP network health report output

7.6 Best Practices Summary

Effective Prompting for ABAP

Aspect Recommendation
SAP Module Specify: MM, SD, FI, PP, etc.
System Version State: ECC 6.0, S/4HANA 2023, ABAP Cloud
Tables/Objects Name specific tables, BAPIs, function modules
Coding Standard Request: Clean ABAP, naming conventions
Error Context Include dump details, error messages, SY-SUBRC values
Output Format Specify: report, class, CDS view, RAP BO

When Kiro Works Best

  • Generating boilerplate code (ALV, CDS, RAP, selection screens)
  • Explaining unfamiliar legacy code
  • Modernizing syntax patterns
  • Identifying common bugs and performance issues
  • Generating unit test scaffolding

When to Verify Carefully

  • Business logic specific to your organization
  • SAP table relationships and field semantics
  • Authorization concepts and security-critical code
  • System-specific customizing dependencies

7.7 Customer Automation Scenarios

Real requests from SAP customers, mapped to how you’d approach each with Kiro + the ABAP Accelerator, and which module’s techniques apply.

Customer scenarioApproach with Kiro + ABAP AcceleratorUses
Functional Spec vs ProgramFeed the FS + ABAP source to Kiro; get a clause-by-clause compliance report (Implemented / Partial / Missing), deviations, and a fix list.Lab 4.4 (Module 4)
Workflow on status changeKiro generates the status-change handler (BAdI / event class / status logic); the Accelerator activates it. You wire the SAP Business Workflow event linkage in SAP.Lab 3.8 (Module 3) · Workflow config is manual
ALV + Variant → Excel → email / shareKiro generates a background job: SUBMIT with the saved variant → XLSX (an available spreadsheet API) → CL_BCS email or OPEN DATASET to a server share.Lab 3.6
Normalize multi-format ExcelKiro generates an ingestion / transform program that maps varied XLSX layouts to one canonical structure, with validation and error rows.Lab 3.7 (Module 3)
Excel macro: ECC 6.0 → Fiori (S/4)Two-sided: on SAP, the Accelerator builds / exposes a released OData (RAP) service; on the client, Kiro rewrites the VBA macro to call OData/HTTPS instead of the old ECC connection.Lab 5.4 (Module 5) · VBA is client-side (Kiro)

Honest scope: the ABAP Accelerator operates on ABAP objects in your SAP system (create, syntax-check, ATC, activate). Client-side pieces — Excel/VBA macros, desktop file handling — are authored by Kiro as a general AI IDE, not by the Accelerator. SAP Business Workflow runtime and ICF/SICF are configured in SAP. Kiro reaches SAP only through ADT / OData — never directly into the database. In this workshop’s demo environment the read/query OData path is a local sap-odata MCP (see the “MCP for SAP ABAP” reference → “Available MCP Servers”); the write path (create / ATC / activate) is the ABAP Accelerator.

Prerequisites & Setup

Most extra setup is ordinary SAP Basis/config. The AWS footprint is small — the AI needs Amazon Bedrock access and the ABAP Accelerator container with a network path to SAP; none of these scenarios need new AWS application services unless you choose to host the mail relay or share drive on AWS.

AWS / infraBedrock model access (required) · a host for the Accelerator container with line-of-sight to SAP · if S/4 runs on AWS: VPC + security groups + VPN/Direct Connect so ADT and OData are reachable · optional: SES (email relay), FSx/EFS/S3 (share drive), ALB + WAF (if exposing OData publicly — security review)
