7.8 Hands-On: Load Excel Data into S/4HANA (Fiori / OData)

Real customer scenario: take the normalized rows from Lab 3.7 and post them into S/4HANA the clean-core way — via a released API, exposed for a Fiori/OData client.

Instructions

  1. Enter the following prompt in Kiro chat:
Generate the ABAP artifacts to load data from Excel into S/4HANA the clean-core way:
- A RAP business object (or use a released BAPI) for the target business entity
- An inbound handler that accepts normalized rows and creates/updates records
  via the RAP behavior (EML: MODIFY ENTITIES) or the released BAPI + BAPI_TRANSACTION_COMMIT
- Field mapping from Excel columns to entity fields, with per-row validation
- A result log: succeeded / failed rows with messages; no partial commits on error
- If RAP-based, expose it for a Fiori/OData client (service definition + binding)
Clean core: released APIs only, no direct table writes.
Then run ATC via the ABAP Accelerator and activate the objects.
  1. Review the generated artifacts
  2. Verify they include:
    • RAP behavior (EML MODIFY ENTITIES) or a released BAPI + commit
    • No direct table writes (clean-core compliant)
    • Field mapping + per-row validation
    • Success/failure result log, no partial commit on error
    • Service definition + binding for OData (if RAP)
  3. Ask the ABAP Accelerator to run ATC and activate the objects.
Expected: ABAP artifacts that post normalized rows into S/4HANA via a RAP behavior (EML MODIFY ENTITIES) or a released BAPI + commit — with field mapping, per-row validation, a success/failure log, and an OData binding for Fiori — ATC-clean and activated.
Setup needed: a RAP behavior (create/update) or a released BAPI; activate the OData service in SICF with auth; client HTTPS access + credentials to the endpoint (same network reachability as Lab 5.4 if S/4 runs on AWS).

Pairs with: Lab 3.7 normalizes the incoming Excel; this lab loads the result into S/4HANA. Together they cover the customer’s “read Excel → save into Fiori (S/4)” scenario end to end. See also 6.3 (REST API Integration).

Capstone prompt — AnyCompany Fiori launchpad (live SAP data)

A real-world build you can run as a use case: a live SAP Fiori launchpad for business users that reads Sales, Finance, and Operations KPIs straight from S/4HANA through the sap-odata MCP (paged $top/$skip reads baked into a snapshot), with drill-down List Report / Object Page pages and a hand-rendered P&L chart.

Show the capstone prompt (copy into Kiro) 
Build a client-side SAP Fiori Launchpad demo web app for "AnyCompany", styled with the
SAPUI5 Fiori Horizon theme (Quartz Light, SAP 72 font, semantic Good/Critical/Error colors).
Put it in a folder called fiori-launchpad/ (index.html, app.js, styles.css, live-data.json).
Load SAPUI5 from the OpenUI5 CDN (sdk.openui5.org), theme sap_horizon, libs
sap.m, sap.ui.core, sap.f, sap.ui.layout, sap.ui.unified ONLY -- do not reference
sap.ushell, sap.viz, or sap.suite.ui.microchart (they 404 on the public CDN and break boot).
Do not use sap.f.SearchManager.

DATA -- everything must come LIVE from SAP, nothing hardcoded. Use the SAP OData MCP tools
to pull the data. If a query is large, fetch it directly from the SAP OData endpoint in
paged batches (use $top + $skip, ~100 rows per page, add $select to keep payloads small)
rather than one big call, because large single responses crash the connection. Bake the
results into live-data.json as a snapshot with a fetchedAt timestamp, and have the app
read that snapshot at load so no tile is ever empty on launch.
Sources:
  - Total Materials:      API_PRODUCT_SRV / A_Product, ProductType eq 'FERT' (count)
  - Low Stock Items:      API_MATERIAL_STOCK_SRV / A_MatlStkInAcctMod, Plant 1710
                          (count where on-hand qty < reorder point; on-hand is live, and
                          since the sandbox has no reorder field, synthesize a deterministic
                          per-material reorder point and label it as demo-derived in the
                          snapshot meta -- do not pass it off as a live field)
  - Open Purchase Orders: API_PURCHASEORDER_PROCESS_SRV / A_PurchaseOrder, CompanyCode 1710,
                          open = PurchasingProcessingStatus 02 or 03
  - Sales Orders + Value: API_SALES_ORDER_SRV / A_SalesOrder, SalesOrganization 1710
                          (count + sum of TotalNetAmount)
  - Revenue/Expenses/P&L: API_JOURNALENTRYITEMBASIC_SRV / A_JournalEntryItemBasic,
                          CompanyCode 1710, Ledger 0L, LedgerFiscalYear 2025,
                          GLAccount 40000000-89999999 (note: field is LedgerFiscalYear,
                          GLAccount is an unpadded 8-digit string; revenue = GL 4xxxxxxx,
                          expenses = GL 5-8xxxxxxx; revenue posts as negative/credit).
                          Aggregate revenue, expenses, and a by-fiscal-period breakdown.

SHELL + CO-BRAND:
  - A thin co-brand strip at the very top (deep navy): the official SAP logo, the word "on",
    the official AWS logo (download both as public-domain SVGs into fiori-launchpad/assets/
    and reference them as local <img>; put the AWS logo on a white rounded chip since its
    wordmark is dark), and a "RISE with SAP" pill on the right.
  - Below it, an SAP Fiori shell bar (sap.f.ShellBar) titled "AnyCompany" with a search
    field, notification bell, and user avatar (initials "AM"). No "S/4HANA on RISE" text.

HOME -- a single launchpad page with a welcome hero header and tiles grouped into three
business "apps":
  - Sales (Order-to-cash): Sales Orders, Order Value
  - Finance (Record-to-report): Revenue FY2025, Profit & Loss (navigation tile)
  - Operations (Materials & procurement): Total Materials, Low Stock Items, Open Purchase Orders
  Each KPI tile shows a live number with its unit and a small footer naming the SAP business
  area (e.g. "Sales & Distribution", "Financial Accounting", "Material Master",
  "Inventory Management", "Procurement") with a green "live" status dot -- do NOT show raw
  OData service names. Color the Low Stock tile red when items are below reorder. If any
  dataset isn't available yet, show "-" with an "awaiting SAP" badge instead of a fake number.
  A snapshot footer shows host, client, and the fetched timestamp.

DRILL-DOWN:
  - Clicking a KPI tile opens a Fiori List Report page: a filter bar with live search and a
    responsive table (demand-popin columns), row count, and semantic status cells.
  - Clicking a row opens a Fiori Object Page with grouped detail sections.
  - Provide List Report + Object Page for Materials, Sales Orders, Open Purchase Orders, and
    Low Stock.

P&L ANALYTICAL PAGE (opens from the Revenue or Profit & Loss tile):
  - A KPI header with Revenue, Expenses, and Net Profit (with margin %), Net Profit card
    tinted green when positive / red when negative.
  - A "Revenue vs Expenses -- FY2025 by period" grouped bar chart built from the live
    by-period data (hand-rendered with HTML/CSS, no chart library), with gridlines, period
    labels, and a legend. Draw the chart only after its container is attached to the DOM
    (retry on animation frames), and guarantee the bars become visible even if the grow-in
    animation frame is missed.

POLISH (make it genuinely Fiori-grade, Operate mode):
  - Horizon design tokens, a clear type scale, tabular numerals for figures, tight-group /
    generous-separation spacing.
  - Theme the browser surfaces too: custom scrollbars, text selection, and focus rings from
    the palette.
  - One restrained motion moment (hero rise, chart grow-in using transform not height/width),
    honoring prefers-reduced-motion.
  - A subtle premium background behind the launchpad (brand-tinted radial wash + faint fading
    grid mesh), kept quiet so tiles stay the focus.
  - Full hover/focus/active/empty/error/loading states, and a single-column phone layout /
    two-up tablet / auto-fill desktop grid with no horizontal overflow.
  - No AI-tell anti-patterns: no thick colored side-border on cards, no emoji standing in for
    icons (draw icons as SVG), no gradient text.
  - Add ?v=<n> cache-busting query strings on app.js and styles.css.

Serve the folder over HTTP (e.g. python3 -m http.server 4173) -- not file:// -- because the
app fetches live-data.json. Verify the final result renders correctly on desktop and mobile
with no console errors before finishing.

Governance from Module 2 still applies: this app only reads SAP via the sap-odata MCP, bakes a snapshot, and writes nothing back — keep business data out of prompts where you can.

Module 8: AI-Driven Development Lifecycle (AI-DLC) with Kiro (45 minutes)

Scope: SAP ABAP on S/4HANA only. This module applies the AI-DLC methodology exclusively to SAP ABAP development — generating ABAP OO classes, CDS views, and RAP-style REST APIs, created and validated in an S/4HANA system via the ABAP Accelerator. The methodology itself is language-agnostic, but every example and lab here is ABAP-specific (no side-by-side BTP/CAP, SAP Build, or other stacks).

Learning Objectives

  • Understand AI-DLC — AWS's development methodology (introduced 2025), now applied to SAP ABAP with Kiro + ABAP Accelerator via AWS for SAP guidance (June 2026)
  • Work through the three AI-DLC phases: Inception → Construction → Operations
  • Build a working SAP S/4HANA application from a plain-language business intent, with AI driving and you approving at each step

8.0 What is AI-DLC?

Earlier modules used AI as an assistant — you drove, the AI helped with isolated tasks. AI-DLC (AI-Driven Development Lifecycle) flips that: the AI initiates the workflow, proposes plans and code, and pauses for your approval at each decision point, while you keep oversight. It is the current AWS-recommended way of working with Kiro and the ABAP Accelerator, published on the AWS for SAP blog in June 2026.

AI-DLC lineage: the methodology was introduced by AWS in 2025 (AI-DLC white paper); its SAP ABAP application is June 2026 AWS for SAP guidance.

Why it matters: AI-assisted development leaves the process human-driven; fully autonomous AI breaks down against enterprise SAP complexity. AI-DLC is the middle path (AI-driven with human validation), designed to take you from business intent to running ABAP in hours instead of weeks.

8.1 The Three Phases

PhaseWhat happensYour role
InceptionAI turns your business intent into elaborated requirements, user stories, and cohesive Units of Work through a collaborative step called Mob Elaboration. It asks clarifying questions; you answer inline.Validate scope, business rules, and edge cases
ConstructionAI proposes architecture and domain models, then generates ABAP through Mob Construction. The ABAP Accelerator creates objects in your SAP system, runs syntax + ATC checks, and activates them.Approve the design and technology choices before code is generated
OperationsAI manages deployment and service configuration (e.g., SICF services) with your oversight.Perform gated manual steps; confirm go-live

What “Mob” means here: both are real-time, whole-team working sessions with the AI in the loop — not the AI running solo.

Mob Elaboration (Inception) — product owner, developers, and architects sit with the AI together to turn a vague business intent into agreed requirements and Units of Work. The AI asks clarifying questions; the group answers and validates on the spot, so ambiguity is resolved before any code exists.

Mob Construction (Construction) — the same collaborative pattern applied to building: the AI proposes architecture, domain models, and ABAP; the group steers technology and design choices and approves each step before generation.

Note on the name: “Mob” borrows the whole-team-together spirit of mob programming — here the “mob” is your team plus the AI, collaborating in real time. It means collaboration and shared validation, not a literal mob-programming ceremony.

Each phase builds on the context of the previous one, and Kiro maintains an audit.md file recording every decision — a persistent trail for review.

Hands-On Lab 8.1: Build a Stock / Inventory Management App from Business Intent

Interactive AI-DLC walkthrough (Archify · click to collapse)

An interactive, self-contained walkthrough of the Lab 8.1 AI-DLC flow generated with the Archify skill, in the workshop palette (orange AI-DLC pipeline, teal Amazon Bedrock model calls, phase-coloured lanes). Trace the flow (PATH), compare roles (LENS), search/zoom, toggle light/dark, and export to PNG/SVG — or click a node to focus it. (A cohesive overview: a few closely-related steps are grouped.)

Prerequisites: Kiro with the ABAP Accelerator MCP server configured (Module 1, Kiro setup), a non-production S/4HANA system with developer authorization, and the AI-DLC steering files set up in your workspace. Select Claude Opus 5 (or the current top-tier Claude Opus model available in your Kiro plan) in the Kiro model selector for best results.

Step 1 — State your business intent

In Kiro chat, paste a natural-language intent describing what to build, the functional scope, technical requirements, and what is explicitly out of scope. Kiro’s Inception phase turns this into a functional specification (elaborated requirements and Units of Work) that you review and approve before any ABAP is generated. For example:

A retailer running SAP S/4HANA wants a stock (inventory) management
application for warehouse and store operations. The system must support:
- Stock overview by material, plant, and storage location
- Goods movements: goods receipt, goods issue, and stock transfer
- Reorder-point checks with low-stock alerts
- Batch and expiry tracking for perishable materials
- Static valuation from the material master
- Stock report export (list + totals)

Technical Requirements:
- SAP HANA database
- ABAP OO backend with business logic classes
- REST APIs via HTTP handlers
- JSON helper utility class
- CDS views for data access

Out of Scope:
- Multi-user roles, warehouse management (EWM), external integrations
- Dynamic valuation, multi-currency, advanced security
Try It

Submit the intent. Kiro recognizes this as a new application request and proposes the first step — requirement analysis. Choose your model and coding mode to proceed.

Kiro chat — AI-DLC Inception: requirement verification questions

Step 2 — Inception: from intent to requirements

  1. Kiro generates a set of requirement verification questions (functional scope, business rules, edge cases, technical constraints) in a file with Answer: tags.
  2. Fill in each Answer: and save. Kiro produces a requirements summary capturing the agreed scope.
  3. On approval, Kiro decomposes the intent into Units of Work — e.g. Stock Overview, Goods Movement, Reorder Management — each with user stories and acceptance criteria.
Expected Output

A requirements summary, a set of Units of Work with acceptance criteria, and an audit.md capturing the decisions so far. You review and approve before moving to Construction.

Step 3 — Construction: from requirements to ABAP

  1. Kiro translates requirements into a technical design using domain-driven design (entities, relationships, patterns). Review this carefully — it's your last checkpoint before code is generated.
  2. With the design approved, Kiro generates the Units of Work in dependency order. The ABAP Accelerator creates the objects directly in your SAP system, runs syntax and ATC checks, and activates them — remediating issues across multiple cycles until clean.
  3. Review the generated ABAP OO classes, CDS views, and HTTP handler REST APIs.

ABAP Accelerator — Construction: object creation + ATC results

If stuck: If ATC flags issues, let the Accelerator iterate

Step 4 — Operations: configure and run

  1. Kiro guides the service configuration (e.g., activating the SICF service for your REST endpoints) with your oversight.
  2. Test the endpoints against your S/4HANA system and confirm the goods-movement flow works end to end.

Validation Checklist

  • Requirements and Units of Work reviewed and approved in the Inception phase
  • Technical design validated before any code generation
  • ABAP objects created, ATC-clean, and activated via the ABAP Accelerator
  • REST service reachable; stock overview and goods-movement operations return expected results
  • audit.md present, documenting decisions across all three phases

Checkpoint

You've applied AI-DLC end to end: business intent → validated requirements → ATC-clean ABAP → a running service, with AI driving and you approving at each gate. This is the target operating model for real SAP ABAP projects on AWS.

Workshop Wrap-Up

Key Takeaways

  1. Kiro accelerates ABAP across the full lifecycle — generate, explain, modernize, debug, and build from intent.
  2. The ABAP Accelerator makes the AI system-aware: it creates, syntax-checks, ATC-validates, and activates objects directly in your SAP system.
  3. AI-DLC turns a plain-language business intent into working, clean-core ABAP through Inception → Construction → Operations, with you approving at each gate.
  4. Clean core is the target: released APIs, ABAP Cloud / RAP, no core modification — upgrade-stable and cloud-ready.
  5. Prompt quality drives output quality — be specific, and always review and test generated code before you activate it.
  6. The real-world customer scenarios (Module 7.7) map directly to labs you can run on your own SAP.

Next Steps

  • Try the laptop-only “generation” mode with Kiro + Amazon Bedrock, then run a proof of concept on your own non-prod S/4HANA.
  • Install the ABAP Accelerator and connect it to a sandbox (see Module 7.7 → “Environment & How to Try This Yourself”).
  • Pick one real backlog item and build it with AI-DLC; share learnings with your SAP team.

Load SAPUI5 from the OpenUI5 CDN (sdk.openui5.org), theme sap_horizon, libs
sap.m, sap.ui.core, sap.f, sap.ui.layout, sap.ui.unified ONLY -- do not reference
sap.ushell, sap.viz, or sap.suite.ui.microchart (they 404 on the public CDN and break boot).
Do not use sap.f.SearchManager.

DATA -- everything must come LIVE from SAP, nothing hardcoded. Use the SAP OData MCP tools
to pull the data. If a query is large, fetch it directly from the SAP OData endpoint in
paged batches (use $top + $skip, ~100 rows per page, add $select to keep payloads small)
rather than one big call, because large single responses crash the connection. Bake the
results into live-data.json as a snapshot with a fetchedAt timestamp, and have the app
read that snapshot at load so no tile is ever empty on launch.
Sources:
  - Total Materials:      API_PRODUCT_SRV / A_Product, ProductType eq 'FERT' (count)
  - Low Stock Items:      API_MATERIAL_STOCK_SRV / A_MatlStkInAcctMod, Plant 1710
                          (count where on-hand qty < reorder point; on-hand is live, and
                          since the sandbox has no reorder field, synthesize a deterministic
                          per-material reorder point and label it as demo-derived in the
                          snapshot meta -- do not pass it off as a live field)
  - Open Purchase Orders: API_PURCHASEORDER_PROCESS_SRV / A_PurchaseOrder, CompanyCode 1710,
                          open = PurchasingProcessingStatus 02 or 03
  - Sales Orders + Value: API_SALES_ORDER_SRV / A_SalesOrder, SalesOrganization 1710
                          (count + sum of TotalNetAmount)
  - Revenue/Expenses/P&L: API_JOURNALENTRYITEMBASIC_SRV / A_JournalEntryItemBasic,
                          CompanyCode 1710, Ledger 0L, LedgerFiscalYear 2025,
                          GLAccount 40000000-89999999 (note: field is LedgerFiscalYear,
                          GLAccount is an unpadded 8-digit string; revenue = GL 4xxxxxxx,
                          expenses = GL 5-8xxxxxxx; revenue posts as negative/credit).
                          Aggregate revenue, expenses, and a by-fiscal-period breakdown.

SHELL + CO-BRAND:
  - A thin co-brand strip at the very top (deep navy): the official SAP logo, the word "on",
    the official AWS logo (download both as public-domain SVGs into fiori-launchpad/assets/
    and reference them as local <img>; put the AWS logo on a white rounded chip since its
    wordmark is dark), and a "RISE with SAP" pill on the right.
  - Below it, an SAP Fiori shell bar (sap.f.ShellBar) titled "AnyCompany" with a search
    field, notification bell, and user avatar (initials "AM"). No "S/4HANA on RISE" text.

HOME -- a single launchpad page with a welcome hero header and tiles grouped into three
business "apps":
  - Sales (Order-to-cash): Sales Orders, Order Value
  - Finance (Record-to-report): Revenue FY2025, Profit & Loss (navigation tile)
  - Operations (Materials & procurement): Total Materials, Low Stock Items, Open Purchase Orders
  Each KPI tile shows a live number with its unit and a small footer naming the SAP business
  area (e.g. "Sales & Distribution", "Financial Accounting", "Material Master",
  "Inventory Management", "Procurement") with a green "live" status dot -- do NOT show raw
  OData service names. Color the Low Stock tile red when items are below reorder. If any
  dataset isn't available yet, show "-" with an "awaiting SAP" badge instead of a fake number.
  A snapshot footer shows host, client, and the fetched timestamp.

DRILL-DOWN:
  - Clicking a KPI tile opens a Fiori List Report page: a filter bar with live search and a
    responsive table (demand-popin columns), row count, and semantic status cells.
  - Clicking a row opens a Fiori Object Page with grouped detail sections.
  - Provide List Report + Object Page for Materials, Sales Orders, Open Purchase Orders, and
    Low Stock.

P&L ANALYTICAL PAGE (opens from the Revenue or Profit & Loss tile):
  - A KPI header with Revenue, Expenses, and Net Profit (with margin %), Net Profit card
    tinted green when positive / red when negative.
  - A "Revenue vs Expenses -- FY2025 by period" grouped bar chart built from the live
    by-period data (hand-rendered with HTML/CSS, no chart library), with gridlines, period
    labels, and a legend. Draw the chart only after its container is attached to the DOM
    (retry on animation frames), and guarantee the bars become visible even if the grow-in
    animation frame is missed.

POLISH (make it genuinely Fiori-grade, Operate mode):
  - Horizon design tokens, a clear type scale, tabular numerals for figures, tight-group /
    generous-separation spacing.
  - Theme the browser surfaces too: custom scrollbars, text selection, and focus rings from
    the palette.
  - One restrained motion moment (hero rise, chart grow-in using transform not height/width),
    honoring prefers-reduced-motion.
  - A subtle premium background behind the launchpad (brand-tinted radial wash + faint fading
    grid mesh), kept quiet so tiles stay the focus.
  - Full hover/focus/active/empty/error/loading states, and a single-column phone layout /
    two-up tablet / auto-fill desktop grid with no horizontal overflow.
  - No AI-tell anti-patterns: no thick colored side-border on cards, no emoji standing in for
    icons (draw icons as SVG), no gradient text.
  - Add ?v=<n> cache-busting query strings on app.js and styles.css.

Serve the folder over HTTP (e.g. python3 -m http.server 4173) -- not file:// -- because the
app fetches live-data.json. Verify the final result renders correctly on desktop and mobile
with no console errors before finishing.

Governance from Module 2 still applies: this app only reads SAP via the sap-odata MCP, bakes a snapshot, and writes nothing back — keep business data out of prompts where you can.

Lab Instructions — Module 3: ABAP Code Generation

Lab 3.1: Generate an ALV Report (MM · Purchase Orders)

Time: 15 minutes

Objective

Use Kiro to generate a complete ALV report from a natural language prompt.

Steps

  1. Open Kiro
  2. Open your Kiro chat panel
  3. Type the following prompt:
Write an ABAP report for S/4HANA that:
- Has a selection screen with parameters for company code (BUKRS) and
  a select-option for document date (AEDAT)
- Reads purchase order headers (EKKO) and items (EKPO) using a JOIN
- Displays results in an ALV grid using CL_SALV_TABLE
- Uses modern ABAP syntax (inline declarations, string templates)
- Follows Clean ABAP naming conventions

(ABAP Accelerator, if connected: then create and activate these objects in my SAP system, running syntax and ATC checks and iterating until clean.)
  1. Review the generated code for:
  2. Selection screen with PARAMETERS and SELECT-OPTIONS
  3. SQL JOIN between EKKO and EKPO
  4. CL_SALV_TABLE for ALV display
  5. Inline declarations (DATA(...))

  6. Error handling (TRY/CATCH)

  7. (Optional) Copy the code to your SAP system and activate it

Validation Checklist

  • Report compiles without syntax errors
  • Selection screen appears with company code and date fields
  • Data is retrieved using a JOIN (not nested SELECTs)
  • ALV grid displays correctly

Troubleshooting

  • If the generated code uses REUSE_ALV_GRID_DISPLAY, ask: "Replace REUSE_ALV with CL_SALV_TABLE"
  • If inline declarations are missing, ask: "Rewrite using inline declarations"

Create an ABAP CDS view entity called ZI_SalesOrderItem that:

  OrderQuantity, NetAmount, Currency, CreationDate

  and I_Material (via VBAP-MATNR)

Lab Instructions — Module 4: Code Explanation & Documentation

Lab 4.1: Explain Legacy Code

Time: 10 minutes

Objective

Use Kiro to understand a legacy ABAP program you've never seen before.

Steps

  1. Copy this code into your Kiro chat:
REPORT z_legacy_sales_report.

TABLES: vbak, vbap, kna1.

DATA: lt_vbak TYPE TABLE OF vbak,
      ls_vbak TYPE vbak,
      lt_vbap TYPE TABLE OF vbap,
      ls_vbap TYPE vbap,
      lv_total TYPE vbap-netwr,
      lv_count TYPE i,
      lt_kna1 TYPE HASHED TABLE OF kna1 WITH UNIQUE KEY kunnr.

SELECT-OPTIONS: s_erdat FOR vbak-erdat,
                s_vkorg FOR vbak-vkorg.

START-OF-SELECTION.

SELECT * FROM vbak INTO TABLE lt_vbak
  WHERE erdat IN s_erdat
    AND vkorg IN s_vkorg
    AND vbtyp = 'C'.

IF lt_vbak IS NOT INITIAL.
  SELECT * FROM kna1 INTO TABLE lt_kna1
    FOR ALL ENTRIES IN lt_vbak
    WHERE kunnr = lt_vbak-kunnr.
ENDIF.

LOOP AT lt_vbak INTO ls_vbak.
  SELECT * FROM vbap INTO TABLE lt_vbap
    WHERE vbeln = ls_vbak-vbeln.
  CLEAR lv_total.
  LOOP AT lt_vbap INTO ls_vbap.
    lv_total = lv_total + ls_vbap-netwr.
    lv_count = lv_count + 1.
  ENDLOOP.
  READ TABLE lt_kna1 INTO DATA(ls_kna1)
    WITH TABLE KEY kunnr = ls_vbak-kunnr.
  WRITE: / ls_vbak-vbeln, ls_vbak-erdat, ls_kna1-name1, lv_total, lv_count.
  CLEAR lv_count.
ENDLOOP.
  1. Ask:
Explain this ABAP code in detail. Describe:
1. The business purpose
2. The data flow
3. Any performance issues
4. Suggestions for improvement
  1. Verify the explanation covers:
    • Purpose: Sales order report filtered by date and sales org
    • VBTYP = 'C' means standard sales orders
    • N+1 problem: SELECT from VBAP inside LOOP
    • Good: Hashed table for customer lookup
    • Missing: Error handling, field list optimization

Lab 4.2: Generate Technical Documentation

Time: 10 minutes

Objective

Auto-generate structured technical documentation for the legacy program.

Steps

  1. Using the same code, prompt:
Generate technical documentation for this ABAP report in the following format:
- Program Name & Description
- Selection Screen Parameters
- Database Tables Used
- Processing Logic (step by step)
- Output Description
- Known Limitations
- Dependencies
  1. Review the documentation for:
    • Accurate program description
    • All selection screen fields listed
    • All 3 tables (VBAK, VBAP, KNA1) mentioned
    • Step-by-step logic matches actual code
    • Limitations include the performance issue

Lab 4.3: Explain Dynamic ABAP

Time: 10 minutes

Objective

Understand dynamic ABAP programming patterns with Kiro's help.

Steps

  1. Provide this code to Kiro:
FIELD-SYMBOLS: <lt_table> TYPE STANDARD TABLE,
               <ls_line>  TYPE any,
               <lv_field> TYPE any.

DATA: lo_descr  TYPE REF TO cl_abap_structdescr,
      lt_comp   TYPE abap_compdescr_tab,
      lr_data   TYPE REF TO data.

lo_descr ?= cl_abap_typedescr=>describe_by_name( iv_table_name ).
lt_comp = lo_descr->components.

CREATE DATA lr_data TYPE TABLE OF (iv_table_name).
ASSIGN lr_data->* TO <lt_table>.

SELECT * FROM (iv_table_name) INTO TABLE <lt_table> UP TO 100 ROWS.

LOOP AT <lt_table> ASSIGNING <ls_line>.
  LOOP AT lt_comp INTO DATA(ls_comp).
    ASSIGN COMPONENT ls_comp-name OF STRUCTURE <ls_line> TO <lv_field>.
    WRITE: / ls_comp-name, ':', <lv_field>.
  ENDLOOP.
ENDLOOP.
  1. Ask:
Explain this dynamic ABAP code. What does it do, and what are the
security implications of using dynamic table names?
  1. Verify the explanation mentions:
    • RTTI (Runtime Type Information) usage
    • Dynamic table creation and data retrieval
    • SQL injection risk with dynamic table names
    • Authority check recommendations

Lab Instructions — Module 5: Modernization & Refactoring

Lab 5.1: Modernize Legacy Code

Time: 15 minutes

Objective

Transform the legacy sales report from Module 4 into modern Clean ABAP.

Steps

  1. Take the legacy code from Lab 4.1
  2. Prompt Kiro:
Refactor this ABAP report to follow Clean ABAP guidelines and modern syntax:
- Use inline declarations
- Replace SELECT * with explicit field lists
- Fix the N+1 SELECT problem (SELECT inside LOOP)
- Use string templates instead of WRITE
- Replace the flat list output with CL_SALV_TABLE
- Use modern ABAP syntax (NEW, VALUE, CORRESPONDING, etc.)
- Add proper error handling with TRY/CATCH
  1. Compare the output against this checklist:
    • All SELECT * replaced with field lists
    • VBAP data retrieved via JOIN or FOR ALL ENTRIES (not inside LOOP)
    • DATA(...) inline declarations used
    • CL_SALV_TABLE for output
    • TRY/CATCH for error handling
    • No TABLES statement
    • No WRITE statements

  2. Ask follow-up: "Can you show me a diff summary of what changed and why?"

Lab 5.2: Clean Core / ABAP Cloud Conversion

Time: 15 minutes

Objective

Convert code to be clean core compliant — using only released APIs for ABAP Cloud / SAP BTP.

Steps

  1. Prompt:
Rewrite this ABAP code to be clean core compliant and compatible with
ABAP Cloud (Tier 1 - released APIs only). Extend without modifying the
core. Replace any unreleased APIs with their released equivalents. The
code should work in SAP BTP ABAP Environment.

Specifically:
- Replace direct database table access with released CDS view consumption
- Use released APIs only
- Follow the ABAP Cloud development model

(ABAP Accelerator, if connected: create/update and activate the changed objects in my SAP system, running ATC with my check variant and iterating until clean.)
  1. Note the key changes:
    • VBAK/VBAP/KNA1 → CDS views like I_SalesOrder, I_SalesOrderItem
    • CL_SALV_TABLE → May need alternative (check released status)
    • WRITE → Not available in ABAP Cloud
    • TABLES statement → Removed entirely

Lab 5.3: FORM to OO Conversion

Time: 15 minutes

Objective

Convert procedural FORM routines to object-oriented methods.

Steps

  1. Provide this code:
FORM calculate_tax USING iv_amount TYPE netwr
                         iv_country TYPE land1
                   CHANGING cv_tax TYPE netwr.
  CASE iv_country.
    WHEN 'DE'. cv_tax = iv_amount * '0.19'.
    WHEN 'US'. cv_tax = iv_amount * '0.08'.
    WHEN 'JP'. cv_tax = iv_amount * '0.10'.
    WHEN OTHERS. cv_tax = iv_amount * '0.15'.
  ENDCASE.
ENDFORM.

FORM get_customer_name USING iv_kunnr TYPE kunnr
                       CHANGING cv_name TYPE name1_gp.
  SELECT SINGLE name1 FROM kna1 INTO cv_name
    WHERE kunnr = iv_kunnr.
ENDFORM.
  1. Prompt:
Convert these FORM routines into a proper ABAP OO class with methods.
Follow Clean ABAP guidelines, use RETURNING parameters where possible,
and add appropriate exception handling.
  1. Verify the output:
    • Class definition with proper visibility sections
    • RETURNING parameters instead of CHANGING where possible
    • Exception class for error handling
    • No FORM/PERFORM statements remain

Lab Instructions — Module 6: Debugging & Troubleshooting

Lab 6.1: Fix a Buggy Program

Time: 10 minutes

Objective

Use Kiro to identify and fix multiple issues in an ABAP program.

Steps

  1. Provide this buggy code to Kiro:
REPORT z_buggy_program.

DATA: lt_items TYPE TABLE OF vbap,
      lt_materials TYPE TABLE OF mara,
      lv_total TYPE p DECIMALS 2.

" Issue 1: SELECT * without WHERE - reads entire table
SELECT * FROM vbap INTO TABLE lt_items.

" Issue 2: SELECT inside LOOP (N+1 problem)
LOOP AT lt_items INTO DATA(ls_item).
  SELECT SINGLE * FROM mara INTO @DATA(ls_mara)
    WHERE matnr = @ls_item-matnr.

  " Issue 3: No SY-SUBRC check after SELECT SINGLE
  lv_total = lv_total + ls_item-netwr * ls_mara-ntgew.

  " Issue 4: READ TABLE without TRANSPORTING NO FIELDS for existence check
  READ TABLE lt_items INTO DATA(ls_check)
    WITH KEY vbeln = ls_item-vbeln
             posnr = ls_item-posnr.
ENDLOOP.

" Issue 5: Division without zero check
DATA(lv_avg) = lv_total / lines( lt_items ).

WRITE: / 'Average:', lv_avg.
  1. Prompt:
This ABAP program has multiple bugs and performance issues.
Identify all issues and provide a corrected version.
  1. Verify Kiro finds all 5 issues:
    • Issue 1: SELECT * without WHERE reads entire VBAP table
    • Issue 2: SELECT SINGLE inside LOOP (N+1 query)
    • Issue 3: No SY-SUBRC check — ls_mara may have initial values
    • Issue 4: READ TABLE copies data unnecessarily
    • Issue 5: Division by zero if lt_items is empty

Lab 6.2: Analyze an ABAP Dump

Time: 10 minutes

Objective

Use Kiro to diagnose a runtime error from ST22.

Steps

  1. Provide this dump context:
I got this ABAP runtime error in production:

Runtime Error: GETWA_NOT_ASSIGNED
Program: Z_PROCESS_ORDERS
Include: Z_PROCESS_ORDERS
Line: 42

Source code extract:
  FIELD-SYMBOLS: <ls_order> TYPE ty_order.
  READ TABLE lt_orders ASSIGNING <ls_order>
    WITH KEY order_id = lv_order_id.
  <ls_order>-status = 'COMPLETED'.    " <-- Line 42

The error occurs intermittently, only for certain order IDs.
What is the cause and how do I fix it?
  1. Verify the response explains:
    • READ TABLE didn't find a matching entry
    • Field symbol <ls_order> is unassigned
    • Accessing an unassigned field symbol causes the dump
    • Fix: check IF sy-subrc = 0 or IF <ls_order> IS ASSIGNED

Lab 6.3: Performance Optimization

Time: 10 minutes

Objective

Optimize a slow-running ABAP program with Kiro's help.

Steps

  1. Provide this code:
" This report takes 30+ minutes to run in production
LOOP AT lt_sales_orders INTO DATA(ls_so).
  LOOP AT lt_deliveries INTO DATA(ls_del)
    WHERE vbeln = ls_so-vbeln.
    LOOP AT lt_billing INTO DATA(ls_bill)
      WHERE vbeln = ls_del-vbeln.
      SELECT SINGLE * FROM bsad INTO @DATA(ls_cleared)
        WHERE bukrs = @ls_bill-bukrs
          AND belnr = @ls_bill-belnr.
      IF sy-subrc = 0.
        APPEND VALUE #(
          vbeln = ls_so-vbeln
          del_no = ls_del-vbeln
          bill_no = ls_bill-vbeln
          cleared = abap_true
        ) TO lt_result.
      ENDIF.
    ENDLOOP.
  ENDLOOP.
ENDLOOP.
  1. Prompt:
This ABAP code takes 30+ minutes in production. Analyze the performance
issues and rewrite it to run efficiently. Explain each optimization.
  1. Expected optimizations:
    • Replace nested LOOPs with sorted tables or secondary keys
    • Move SELECT out of loop — use FOR ALL ENTRIES or JOIN
    • Consider replacing entire structure with a single SQL JOIN
    • Use parallel cursor technique if nested LOOPs remain

(ABAP Accelerator, if connected: create/update and activate the changed objects in my SAP system, running ATC with my check variant and iterating until clean.)

Clean Core / ABAP Cloud Compliance

Rewrite this code to be clean core compliant — extend without modifying
the core, using only released (Tier 1) APIs compatible with SAP BTP
ABAP Environment / ABAP Cloud.

Modernization Quick Reference

Legacy Modern
DATA: lv TYPE ... then assign DATA(lv) = ...
CONCATENATE a b INTO c c = \|{ a }{ b }\|
CREATE OBJECT lo lo = NEW #( )
CALL METHOD lo->m lo->m( )
SELECT * SELECT field1, field2
REUSE_ALV_* CL_SALV_TABLE
FORM/PERFORM Class methods
MOVE a TO b b = a

Common ABAP Dumps & Fixes

Dump Cause Fix
GETWA_NOT_ASSIGNED Field symbol not assigned Check IS ASSIGNED after READ TABLE
ITAB_DUPLICATE_KEY Duplicate key in hashed/sorted table Check before INSERT or use STANDARD TABLE
COMPUTE_INT_ZERODIVIDE Division by zero Check divisor ≠ 0 before dividing
DBIF_RSQL_SQL_ERROR SQL error Check SQL syntax, field types
TSV_TNEW_PAGE_ALLOC_FAILED Out of memory Reduce data volume, use pagination

Key SAP Tables Reference

Area Header Table Item Table
Sales Orders VBAK VBAP
Purchase Orders EKKO EKPO
Deliveries LIKP LIPS
Billing VBRK VBRP
Material Master MARA MARC, MARD
Business Partner BUT000 BUT020
Accounting BKPF BSEG (use CDS in S/4)

Lab Instructions — MCP for SAP ABAP

Estimated time: 20–25 minutes
If you get stuck: Skip this lab and move to the next one. You can always come back later. The labs are independent of each other.

Lab MCP.1: Read SAP Objects via Chat

Time: 5 minutes

Objective

Use natural language prompts to read ABAP source code and table definitions directly from SAP — without copy-pasting.

Exercise A — Read a program

Type this in your AI chat:

Read the source code of the ABAP demo program SAPBC_DATA_GENERATOR and explain what it does.
Expected: The AI calls get_program_source, retrieves the code, and gives you a summary — all without you pasting anything

Exercise B — Explore a table structure

Get the structure of table SCARR (airline carriers). Then write a modern ABAP SELECT that reads all carriers and displays them in an ALV grid.
Expected: The AI calls get_table_source for SCARR, sees the fields (CARRID, CARRNAME, CURRCODE, URL), and generates a working ABAP report

Exercise C — Read table data

Show me the first 5 rows from table SCARR.
Expected: The AI calls get_table_contents with max_rows=5 and shows you actual data like AA/American Airlines, LH/Lufthansa, etc.

Lab MCP.2: Advanced — Where-Used and Cross-Object Analysis

Time: 10 minutes

Objective

Use MCP tools for cross-object analysis that would normally require multiple SAP transactions.

Exercise A — Where-used analysis

Find all objects that reference function module POPUP_TO_CONFIRM. List the top 5 and explain how each one uses it.
Expected: The AI calls get_usage_references and returns a list of programs/classes that call this FM, with context on each usage

Exercise B — Search and compare

Search for all ABAP objects matching "SFLIGHT*". Then read the source of program SAPBC_DATA_GENERATOR and the structure of table SFLIGHT. Explain how they relate to each other.
Expected: The AI chains multiple MCP calls — search_objects, get_program_source, get_table_source — and synthesizes the results

Exercise C — Generate code using live SAP context

This is where it pays off: the AI reads your actual SAP system to generate accurate code:

Read the structure of tables EKKO and EKPO from my SAP system. Then write a complete ABAP report that:
1. Has a selection screen for company code and document date range
2. JOINs these two tables using the actual field names you found
3. Displays results in CL_SALV_TABLE
4. Uses modern ABAP syntax
Expected: The AI reads both table structures via MCP, uses the real field names (not guessed ones), and generates a report with correct JOINs
Key Takeaway: Without MCP, you'd need to copy-paste table structures into the chat. With MCP, the AI reads them directly — and the generated code uses actual field names from your system, not hallucinated ones.

Troubleshooting — MCP Lab
The AI doesn't use MCP tools — it just answers from memory
Make sure the MCP server shows as "Connected" in your IDE. If tools are set to "Ask" permission, you need to approve each tool call when prompted.
get_table_contents returns empty
The table might be empty in your system. Try SCARR or SFLIGHT — these are SAP demo tables that usually have data. If using a fresh system, run program SAPBC_DATA_GENERATOR first.
Timeout on large programs
Some SAP standard programs are huge (100K+ lines). Try smaller programs first, or increase the timeout to 120 seconds in your MCP config.
Authorization error on where-used
Where-used analysis requires additional ADT authorizations. Ask your Basis admin to check S_ADT_RES and S_DEVELOP authorization objects.

MCP for SAP ABAP — Connect Your IDE to SAP

The Model Context Protocol (MCP) is an open standard that lets AI assistants (Kiro, Claude) connect directly to external tools and data sources. For SAP ABAP, this means your AI assistant can read source code, table structures, and data directly from your SAP system — no copy-pasting needed.

Why MCP matters for ABAP developers:
  • Ask "explain program SAPMV45A" → AI reads the source code directly from SAP
  • Ask "what fields are in table VBAK?" → AI queries the table definition live
  • Ask "find all programs that use BAPI_SALESORDER_CREATEFROMDAT2" → AI runs where-used analysis
  • No more copy-pasting code into chat — the AI fetches it automatically

Available MCP Servers for SAP ABAP

Which AWS SAP MCP server for what? (three different tools)

AWS offers three MCP servers in the SAP space — they solve different problems. The first two are developer-time tools you can use together; the third is a runtime tool for agents. Don't confuse them:

MCP serverPurposeSetup
ABAP Accelerator
(Jan 2026)		System-aware development. Connects to your SAP system via ADT to read/generate/validate ABAP, run ATC checks, activate objects, and convert ECC→S/4HANA.Free Docker image you run locally; needs SAP connection + credentials
AWS SDK for SAP ABAP Knowledge MCP Server
(GA Apr 2026)		AWS-integration know-how. Feeds your IDE the authoritative AWS SDK for SAP ABAP docs (130,000+ pages) so it writes correct ABAP to call AWS services like Amazon S3, Bedrock, and Textract.Hosted HTTPS endpoint — no auth, no AWS account, no local install; just add the URL
AWS for SAP MCP Server
(GA May 2026)		Runtime business-data agents (not a dev tool). Lets an AI agent read and write SAP business data (orders, invoices, materials) via OData — for building agentic apps on top of SAP, not for writing ABAP.Managed on Amazon Bedrock AgentCore Runtime; deploy via CloudFormation (OAuth 2.0 auth)

Rule of thumb: use ABAP Accelerator to write and validate ABAP against your live system; add the SDK Knowledge MCP Server whenever that ABAP needs to call an AWS service; reach for the managed AWS for SAP MCP Server only when you're building an AI agent that reads/writes SAP business data at runtime. This workshop focuses on the first two (developer tooling). SDK Knowledge MCP announcement ↗ · AWS for SAP MCP Server docs ↗

Recommended: AWS ABAP Accelerator (official)

In January 2026, AWS launched ABAP Accelerator — an official MCP server for SAP ABAP development that works with Kiro across the entire software-development lifecycle: create, test, document, and transform ABAP. It is a free downloadable Docker image that connects to your SAP system via standard ADT, and integrates directly with the SAP ABAP Test Cockpit (ATC) to validate generated code, fetch included custom code, and reduce AI "hallucinations". Read the announcement ↗ · GitHub repo ↗

  • Automated ECC → S/4HANA code conversion — converts legacy ABAP while preserving business logic, validated against ATC
  • ATC-validated generation — runs syntax checks, ATC with your custom variants, object activation, and transport-request management; iterates until issues (syntax, security, performance, naming) are resolved
  • Test-Driven Development — generates unit tests to baseline current behavior before changing code, de-risking transformations
  • Clean core development — generates RAP artifacts (CDS views, behavior definitions, service definitions/bindings) and even full Fiori apps from a single prompt
  • Always-current documentation — embeds docs directly in the SAP objects it creates or modifies
  • AI-assisted error resolution — analyzes ST22 dumps, job logs, and error messages to find root causes

Why it matters (business bottom line): fewer manual hours on S/4HANA conversions, higher first-time code quality (fewer debugging cycles), lower transformation risk through permanent regression test suites, faster clean-core / RAP adoption, documentation that never drifts from the code, and faster incident resolution with fewer escalations. Source: AWS for SAP blog, Jan 2026.

Within Kiro CLI, ABAP Accelerator can perform mass code analysis and conversion across many objects at once — ideal for clean core cleanup at scale.

Set up the ABAP Accelerator MCP server (hands-on)

These are the concrete steps to connect Kiro to the official ABAP Accelerator from the AWS Solutions Library guidance repo. The repo runs as a local Python HTTP (streamable-http) MCP server on localhost:8000 and connects to your SAP system over ADT. (The same project is also published as a container image — this hands-on uses the Python path, which is handy on a laptop.)

Prerequisites: Python 3.10+ (macOS system Python 3.9 is too old — install a newer one, e.g. brew install python@3.13), git, network access to your SAP system, and an SAP developer user.

1 — Clone the repo

git clone https://github.com/aws-solutions-library-samples/guidance-for-deploying-sap-abap-accelerator-for-amazon-q-developer.git abap-accelerator
cd abap-accelerator

2 — Create a Python 3.10+ virtual environment & install

python3.13 -m venv .venv              # use any Python >= 3.10
.venv/bin/python -m pip install --upgrade pip
.venv/bin/pip install -r requirements.txt

3 — Create the .env (replace the placeholders)

SAP_HOST=YOUR_SAP_HOST            # bare host or IP — no https:// and no port
SAP_INSTANCE_NUMBER=00            # secure URL = 44300 + instance, so port 44300 → instance 00
SAP_CLIENT=100
SAP_USERNAME=YOUR_USER
SAP_PASSWORD='YOUR_PASSWORD'      # single-quote if it contains $ or other shell-special chars
SAP_LANGUAGE=EN
SAP_SECURE=true
SERVER_HOST=localhost
SERVER_PORT=8000
SSL_VERIFY=false                  # DEMO ONLY (self-signed cert) — use true + a trusted cert in production; see "Securing credentials" below
LOG_LEVEL=INFO
Three things that silently break auth: (1) a password containing $ must be single-quoted or the shell truncates it; (2) a demo SAP on EC2 usually presents a self-signed cert — set SSL_VERIFY=false or the connection fails on cert verification (demo only — see Securing credentials below); (3) the server rebuilds the URL as 44300 + SAP_INSTANCE_NUMBER when secure, so match the instance to your port. Keep .env out of git (it is in the repo’s .gitignore).

Securing credentials (don’t ship a basic-auth .env to production)

The .env above uses basic auth (SAP user + password) and SSL_VERIFY=false. That is fine for a local demo against a throwaway, non-production system, but harden it before anything real:

  • Don’t keep a long-lived password in a file. Pull the SAP credentials from a secret store at launch and export them into the server’s environment instead of committing them — AWS Secrets Manager (fetch in your start script, e.g. aws secretsmanager get-secret-value), the SAP Credential Store, or your OS keychain. The server only ever sees them as process environment variables.
  • Prefer token / certificate auth over basic auth where the connector supports it — OAuth2 / SAP BTP JWT (the mcp-adt server supports this) or X.509 client certificates for ADT — so no static password is stored at all. Check each server’s README for its supported auth methods.
  • Use a least-privilege technical developer user scoped to ADT on a non-production system — never a personal dialog user, never an admin, never production.
  • Keep TLS verification on in production (SSL_VERIFY=true) with a CA-trusted certificate. SSL_VERIFY=false is only acceptable against a self-signed demo host and should never ship.
  • Lock down the local server: bind it to localhost only, restrict file permissions on the .env, keep it git-ignored, avoid verbose logging of secrets, and rotate the credential regularly.
Rule of thumb for a customer environment: secret store + least-privilege technical user + token/cert auth + TLS on + localhost-bound server. The plaintext .env with SSL_VERIFY=false shown above is a demo convenience, not a production pattern.

4 — Start the server (keep it running)

.venv/bin/python src/aws_abap_accelerator/main.py
This is a long-running HTTP server on localhost:8000, not a stdio process — leave it up for the whole session and restart it after a reboot. Right after starting, make one call (e.g. ask Kiro for connection_status) to warm the SAP session; a long-idle session expires (“Session Timed Out”) and needs a restart.

5 — Register it in Kiro

Add inside mcpServers in ~/.kiro/settings/mcp.json (back the file up first). This server connects by URL, not by launching a command:

{
  "mcpServers": {
    "abap-accelerator": {
      "url": "http://localhost:8000/mcp",
      "disabled": false,
      "autoApprove": []
    }
  }
}

Wait — if the URL says localhost, how does Kiro reach my SAP system?

localhost:8000 is not your SAP system — it is the ABAP Accelerator MCP server running on your own machine. There are two separate hops, and Kiro only ever makes the first one:

Kiro  --MCP over HTTP-->  ABAP Accelerator MCP server  --HTTPS / ADT-->  Your SAP system
(the AI)                 (local bridge · localhost:8000)              (e.g. your-s4h:44300)
  • Hop 1 — Kiro → MCP server. mcp.json only tells Kiro where the MCP server is (http://localhost:8000/mcp). Nothing about SAP — no host, no password — is in this file.
  • Hop 2 — MCP server → SAP. The server holds the SAP target and credentials in its own .env (host, instance/port, client, user, auth) and makes authenticated ADT calls over HTTPS. The SAP password lives here, never in mcp.json — Kiro never sees it.

So the MCP server is a local bridge: Kiro speaks MCP to it over loopback, and it translates that into authenticated ADT/HTTPS calls to SAP and relays results back. Stop that local process and your abap-accelerator tools go dead even though mcp.json is unchanged — hop 1 has nothing listening behind it. A managed deployment follows the same client → server → SAP split, except the server runs on Amazon Bedrock AgentCore Runtime instead of localhost (AWS for SAP MCP Server docs).

6 — Verify

Ask Kiro to call connection_status.

Expected: “SAP Connection Status: Connected” with your host, instance, client, language, and user — the Accelerator tools are now available in Kiro.

Tools it exposes: connection_status, get_objects, create_object, get_source, update_source, check_syntax, activate_object, activate_objects_batch, run_atc_check, run_unit_tests, create_or_update_test_class, get_test_classes, search_object, get_migration_analysis, get_transport_requests.

Running ABAP from the IDE — the unit-test harness pattern

The Accelerator is a development server, not an execution engine: it reads, writes, syntax-checks, activates, and ATC/unit-tests ABAP, but has no “run report / run transaction” tool, so it cannot directly run a classic report and return its ALV output.

To actually execute ABAP and see real output, use run_unit_tests as a runner: put the logic in a class method, call it from a test method, and surface the computed values through a tolerable-level assertion — cl_abap_unit_assert=>fail( msg = lv_output level = if_aunit_constants=>tolerable ). ABAP Unit only returns a message when an assertion fires, so the “failure” is simply the delivery vehicle for your output; the runner executes the ABAP on SAP and returns the real values. (Create the class in $TMP so no transport is needed.)

Quick pick: which MCP server for this workshop?

ServerRead or write?Best forRuns where
ABAP Accelerator (AWS)Write — create, syntax, ATC, activateThe full system-aware ABAP dev loop from any MCP IDE (Kiro)AWS Docker image you run locally; connects to SAP via ADT
SAP ADT MCP Server (SAP)Write — create, ATC, RAP, activateTeams already working in ADT for VS Code (native, no extra container)Built into the ADT for VS Code extension (port 2236); experimental
sap-odata (local)Read / query onlyShowing live SAP business data (materials, stock, OData) in chatLocal Node server calling your SAP OData services

Details for each are below. All three connect to your SAP system and never reach the database directly.

Official SAP MCP servers & the wider ecosystem

SAP now publishes its own MCP servers too. The one most relevant to ABAP teams is SAP’s ADT MCP Server, which exposes the ADT capabilities of ABAP Development Tools for VS Code to MCP clients (setup via the SAP Help Portal). SAP also ships MCP servers for Fiori app generation, CAP, UI5 / UI5 Web Components, the Mobile Development Kit, BTP administration, and SAP LeanIX.

On top of that is a fast-growing community ecosystem — ABAP/ADT bridges, OData & Gateway, Cloud Integration (CPI), HANA & analytics, SAP GUI automation, and docs/knowledge servers. A regularly-updated, curated catalog lives at github.com/marianfoo/sap-ai-mcp-servers (browsable at sap-ai-tools.marianzeis.de).

One community server worth knowing for clean core: ROSA (ClementRingot/ROSA) gives an AI agent real-time knowledge of which SAP objects are released for ABAP Cloud / clean core — and what to use instead when they are not.

Community MCP Servers (alternatives)

If you cannot run the AWS ABAP Accelerator, several community MCP servers also connect to SAP via ADT (ABAP Development Tools) services (some well-known examples below; see the catalog above for the full, current list):

ServerLanguageAuthKey Features
mcp-abap-adt
GitHub ↗		 Node.js Basic (user/pass) Get programs, classes, functions, tables, table contents, search objects, interfaces, transactions
mcp-adt
GitHub ↗		 Python Basic + BTP (JWT) All of the above + CDS views, metadata extensions, freestyle SQL queries, where-used references, enhancement discovery, BTP support
Vibing Steampunk
GitHub ↗		 — ADT ADT-to-MCP bridge for ABAP and AMDP workflows; the most-starred community ABAP MCP.
ARC-1
GitHub ↗		 — BTP OAuth Secure-by-default, enterprise-ready ABAP MCP for IDEs and Copilot via the ADT REST API.
These are community-maintained open-source projects. Review the code and security implications before connecting to production SAP systems.

Read SAP business data via a local OData MCP (sap-odata)

A lightweight alternative for reading SAP business data (materials, stock, any OData entity) straight into your IDE chat is a small self-hosted MCP server that calls your SAP OData services. In this workshop's demo environment it is registered in ~/.kiro/settings/mcp.json as sap-odata (a local Node server, node .../sap-odata-mcp-setup/server.mjs).

It is read/query oriented over OData — distinct from the ABAP Accelerator, which writes and activates ABAP objects via ADT. Use it to show live SAP data alongside AI-assisted development.

ToolWhat it does
search_materialsSearch for materials by number or description
get_material_stockGet current stock levels for materials
run_odata_queryRun a custom OData query against any SAP service
Expected: In Kiro chat, “search materials for pumps” or “show current stock for material X” returns live rows from your SAP system via OData — no ABAP written or activated.
This is a read-oriented OData connection: it does not create, syntax-check, ATC-validate, or activate ABAP. For system-aware ABAP development (write path) use the ABAP Accelerator. Set the server's autoApprove for its read tools if you want a click-free live demo.
Capstone prompt — AnyCompany Fiori launchpad (live SAP data)

Everything above is read-only OData. Hand Kiro this spec to see what those same sap-odata tools build end to end: a live SAP Fiori launchpad for “AnyCompany” — KPI tiles, drill-down List Report / Object Page pages, and a hand-rendered P&L chart — all from paged $top/$skip reads baked into a snapshot.

Show the capstone prompt (copy into Kiro) 
Build a client-side SAP Fiori Launchpad demo web app for "AnyCompany", styled with the
SAPUI5 Fiori Horizon theme (Quartz Light, SAP 72 font, semantic Good/Critical/Error colors).
Put it in a folder called fiori-launchpad/ (index.html, app.js, styles.css, live-data.json).
Load SAPUI5 from the OpenUI5 CDN (sdk.openui5.org), theme sap_horizon, libs
sap.m, sap.ui.core, sap.f, sap.ui.layout, sap.ui.unified ONLY -- do not reference
sap.ushell, sap.viz, or sap.suite.ui.microchart (they 404 on the public CDN and break boot).
Do not use sap.f.SearchManager.

DATA -- everything must come LIVE from SAP, nothing hardcoded. Use the SAP OData MCP tools
to pull the data. If a query is large, fetch it directly from the SAP OData endpoint in
paged batches (use $top + $skip, ~100 rows per page, add $select to keep payloads small)
rather than one big call, because large single responses crash the connection. Bake the
results into live-data.json as a snapshot with a fetchedAt timestamp, and have the app
read that snapshot at load so no tile is ever empty on launch.
Sources:
  - Total Materials:      API_PRODUCT_SRV / A_Product, ProductType eq 'FERT' (count)
  - Low Stock Items:      API_MATERIAL_STOCK_SRV / A_MatlStkInAcctMod, Plant 1710
                          (count where on-hand qty < reorder point; on-hand is live, and
                          since the sandbox has no reorder field, synthesize a deterministic
                          per-material reorder point and label it as demo-derived in the
                          snapshot meta -- do not pass it off as a live field)
  - Open Purchase Orders: API_PURCHASEORDER_PROCESS_SRV / A_PurchaseOrder, CompanyCode 1710,
                          open = PurchasingProcessingStatus 02 or 03
  - Sales Orders + Value: API_SALES_ORDER_SRV / A_SalesOrder, SalesOrganization 1710
                          (count + sum of TotalNetAmount)
  - Revenue/Expenses/P&L: API_JOURNALENTRYITEMBASIC_SRV / A_JournalEntryItemBasic,
                          CompanyCode 1710, Ledger 0L, LedgerFiscalYear 2025,
                          GLAccount 40000000-89999999 (note: field is LedgerFiscalYear,
                          GLAccount is an unpadded 8-digit string; revenue = GL 4xxxxxxx,
                          expenses = GL 5-8xxxxxxx; revenue posts as negative/credit).
                          Aggregate revenue, expenses, and a by-fiscal-period breakdown.

SHELL + CO-BRAND:
  - A thin co-brand strip at the very top (deep navy): the official SAP logo, the word "on",
    the official AWS logo (download both as public-domain SVGs into fiori-launchpad/assets/
    and reference them as local <img>; put the AWS logo on a white rounded chip since its
    wordmark is dark), and a "RISE with SAP" pill on the right.
  - Below it, an SAP Fiori shell bar (sap.f.ShellBar) titled "AnyCompany" with a search
    field, notification bell, and user avatar (initials "AM"). No "S/4HANA on RISE" text.

HOME -- a single launchpad page with a welcome hero header and tiles grouped into three
business "apps":
  - Sales (Order-to-cash): Sales Orders, Order Value
  - Finance (Record-to-report): Revenue FY2025, Profit & Loss (navigation tile)
  - Operations (Materials & procurement): Total Materials, Low Stock Items, Open Purchase Orders
  Each KPI tile shows a live number with its unit and a small footer naming the SAP business
  area (e.g. "Sales & Distribution", "Financial Accounting", "Material Master",
  "Inventory Management", "Procurement") with a green "live" status dot -- do NOT show raw
  OData service names. Color the Low Stock tile red when items are below reorder. If any
  dataset isn't available yet, show "-" with an "awaiting SAP" badge instead of a fake number.
  A snapshot footer shows host, client, and the fetched timestamp.

DRILL-DOWN:
  - Clicking a KPI tile opens a Fiori List Report page: a filter bar with live search and a
    responsive table (demand-popin columns), row count, and semantic status cells.
  - Clicking a row opens a Fiori Object Page with grouped detail sections.
  - Provide List Report + Object Page for Materials, Sales Orders, Open Purchase Orders, and
    Low Stock.

P&L ANALYTICAL PAGE (opens from the Revenue or Profit & Loss tile):
  - A KPI header with Revenue, Expenses, and Net Profit (with margin %), Net Profit card
    tinted green when positive / red when negative.
  - A "Revenue vs Expenses -- FY2025 by period" grouped bar chart built from the live
    by-period data (hand-rendered with HTML/CSS, no chart library), with gridlines, period
    labels, and a legend. Draw the chart only after its container is attached to the DOM
    (retry on animation frames), and guarantee the bars become visible even if the grow-in
    animation frame is missed.

POLISH (make it genuinely Fiori-grade, Operate mode):
  - Horizon design tokens, a clear type scale, tabular numerals for figures, tight-group /
    generous-separation spacing.
  - Theme the browser surfaces too: custom scrollbars, text selection, and focus rings from
    the palette.
  - One restrained motion moment (hero rise, chart grow-in using transform not height/width),
    honoring prefers-reduced-motion.
  - A subtle premium background behind the launchpad (brand-tinted radial wash + faint fading
    grid mesh), kept quiet so tiles stay the focus.
  - Full hover/focus/active/empty/error/loading states, and a single-column phone layout /
    two-up tablet / auto-fill desktop grid with no horizontal overflow.
  - No AI-tell anti-patterns: no thick colored side-border on cards, no emoji standing in for
    icons (draw icons as SVG), no gradient text.
  - Add ?v=<n> cache-busting query strings on app.js and styles.css.

Serve the folder over HTTP (e.g. python3 -m http.server 4173) -- not file:// -- because the
app fetches live-data.json. Verify the final result renders correctly on desktop and mobile
with no console errors before finishing.

Governance from Module 2 still applies: this app only reads SAP via the sap-odata MCP, bakes a snapshot, and writes nothing back — keep business data out of prompts where you can.

Option: SAP’s built-in ADT MCP Server (VS Code)

If your team works in ABAP Development Tools for VS Code, SAP now ships a built-in ADT MCP Server — a local HTTP server (default port 2236) that runs inside the ADT extension and exposes ABAP development tools to any MCP-compatible AI assistant (GitHub Copilot is confirmed; other agents that support VS Code’s virtual workspace filesystem also work). It is a write-capable, system-aware path like the ABAP Accelerator, but native to SAP’s own VS Code tooling.

What its tools can do: create objects and packages, generate RAP applications, activate objects, run ABAP Test Cockpit (ATC) and apply AI fixes, run ABAP Unit tests, and create / read transport requests (e.g. abap_creation-create_object, abap_generators-generate_objects, abap_activate_objects, abap_atc_run, abap_run_unit_tests, abap_transport-create).

Prerequisites: VS Code + the ABAP Development Tools for VS Code extension, and access to an ABAP Cloud system — SAP BTP ABAP environment, SAP S/4HANA Cloud ABAP environment, or SAP S/4HANA (release 2025 or higher). A free SAP BTP ABAP environment trial works.

Enable it

  1. Install the ABAP Development Tools for Visual Studio Code extension.
  2. Open Settings (Cmd/Ctrl+Shift+P → “Preferences: Open Settings (UI)”), search adt mcp, and enable Adt: Enable MCP Server (or in JSON: "adt.mcpServer.enabled": true). Default port is 2236.
  3. Add your system to the workspace via ABAP: Add Destination as Folder to the Workspace — the MCP server only starts once a destination is active.
  4. Reload VS Code. Confirm the status bar shows “ADT MCP Server running on port 2236”, or run >MCP: List Servers from the Command Palette.
  5. In your coding agent’s Agent mode → Configure Tools, confirm the ADT MCP Server tools are listed and enabled.
Expected: In your agent’s Agent-mode chat, “List all available ABAP RAP generators using the MCP tool” returns generator names (e.g., “OData UI Service from Scratch”) — confirming the ADT MCP Server is connected.
SAP labels the ADT MCP Server an experimental feature that may change without notice and is not intended for productive use — use a non-production system and review SAP’s security recommendations. ADT MCP tools appear only in the agent’s Agent mode (not Ask / Plan). Docs: SAP tutorial.

Prerequisites

  • SAP system with ADT services enabled (service /sap/bc/adt active in SICF)
  • SAP user with authorization for ADT access
  • Network connectivity from your machine to the SAP system
  • Node.js 18+ (for mcp-abap-adt) or Python 3.9+ (for mcp-adt)

Install the MCP server

Step 1 — Clone and install the server

Choose one of the two servers. We'll use mcp-adt (Python) as it has more features:

Which server is this? mcp-adt and mcp-abap-adt are community open-source MCP servers — great for a laptop demo when you don't have the AWS Accelerator set up. They are not the official AWS tooling. For the full system-aware loop (create → syntax → ATC → activate) and the governance controls used later in this workshop, use the official AWS ABAP Accelerator setup above. The lab steps are nearly identical — keep this community path only as a fallback.

git clone https://github.com/YahorNovik/mcp-adt.git
cd mcp-adt
python -m venv .venv
source .venv/bin/activate    # macOS/Linux
# .venv\Scripts\activate   # Windows
pip install -r requirements.txt

Step 2 — Configure SAP connection

Create a .env file in the mcp-adt directory:

# .env file — replace with your SAP system details
SAP_AUTH_TYPE=basic
SAP_URL=https://your-sap-system:443
SAP_CLIENT=100
SAP_USER=YOUR_USERNAME
SAP_PASS=YOUR_PASSWORD
SAP_VERIFY_SSL=true
Secure these credentials. The .env above is basic auth for a non-production demo. For a customer environment, pull the SAP credentials from a secret store (AWS Secrets Manager / SAP Credential Store / OS keychain) instead of a committed file; prefer token/cert auth (mcp-adt supports BTP JWT) over a stored password; use a least-privilege non-production user; keep TLS verification on; and never commit .env (git-ignore it). See Securing credentials above for the full checklist.

Add the MCP server to Kiro

Configure in Kiro

Add the MCP server to your Kiro configuration at ~/.kiro/settings/mcp.json:

{
  "mcpServers": {
    "sap-abap-adt": {
      "command": "python",
      "args": ["/full/path/to/mcp-adt/mcp_server.py"],
      "timeout": 60
    }
  }
}

Kiro will auto-detect the MCP tools and make them available in chat.

Available MCP Tools

Once connected, these tools are available to your AI assistant:

ToolWhat It DoesExample Prompt
get_program_sourceRead ABAP program source code"Explain program SAPMV45A"
get_class_sourceRead ABAP class source"Show me class CL_SALV_TABLE"
get_function_sourceRead function module source"What does FM BAPI_SALESORDER_CREATEFROMDAT2 do?"
get_table_sourceRead table definition"What fields are in VBAK?"
get_table_contentsFetch table data (max 100 rows)"Show me 10 rows from SCARR"
get_cds_sourceRead CDS view definition"Explain CDS view I_SalesOrder"
get_usage_referencesWhere-used analysis"Where is BAPI_MATERIAL_GETLIST used?"
search_objectsSearch for ABAP objects"Find all Z* programs in package ZWORKSHOP"
get_sql_queryRun freestyle SQL"Count sales orders by status in VBAK"

Read-only vs. write-capable: The tools above (read source, table contents, where-used) are the common read tools shared by the community MCP servers. The official ABAP Accelerator goes further — it is write-capable and system-aware, able to create, update, syntax-check, unit-test, ATC-validate, and activate objects directly in your SAP system. That write path is what powers AI-DLC's Construction phase and the ECC→S/4HANA conversion.

ABAP Accelerator MCP tools (write-capable)

Beyond the read tools, the ABAP Accelerator exposes the following tools (tool names may evolve; check the repo README for the current set):

ToolWhat It Does
aws_abap_cb_create_objectCreate a new ABAP object in the SAP system
aws_abap_cb_update_sourceUpdate the source code of an existing object
aws_abap_cb_get_sourceRead an object's source, including includes and references
aws_abap_cb_search_objectSearch objects by pattern or keyword
aws_abap_cb_check_syntaxRun a syntax check before activation
aws_abap_cb_activate_objectActivate an object once syntax is clean
aws_abap_cb_create_or_update_test_classCreate or update an ABAP Unit test class
aws_abap_cb_run_unit_testsRun ABAP Unit tests and return the results
aws_abap_cb_run_atc_checkRun an ABAP Test Cockpit (ATC) quality check against a check variant

The create → syntax-check → activate → unit-test → ATC loop is what lets the Accelerator iterate on its own generated code until it is clean, reducing AI "hallucinations" compared with a read-only MCP server.

Try It Now

Once your MCP server is connected, try these prompts:

Warm-Up: Read a program
Read the source code of program SAPMV45A and explain what it does in 3 bullet points.
Explore a table
Get the structure of table VBAK and write an ABAP SELECT that joins it with VBAP to get sales order items with material descriptions.
Where-used analysis
Find all programs that call function module BAPI_SALESORDER_CREATEFROMDAT2 and summarize how each one uses it.

Troubleshooting

MCP Troubleshooting
MCP server won't connect
Check that the SAP system URL is reachable from your machine. Try curl https://your-sap-system:443/sap/bc/adt/discovery — you should get an XML response. Also verify the /sap/bc/adt service is active in SICF.
Authentication error (401)
Double-check your username, password, and client number in the .env file. If your password contains special characters like #, wrap it in quotes.
Tools show up but return empty results
Your SAP user may lack authorization for ADT services. Ask your Basis admin to check authorizations for the S_ADT_RES authorization object.
Timeout errors on large programs
Increase the timeout in your MCP config from 60 to 120 seconds. Large programs like SAPMV45A can take time to retrieve.
SSL certificate errors
If your SAP system uses self-signed certificates, set SAP_VERIFY_SSL=false in your .env file (not recommended for production).

SAP/ABAP Glossary & Cheat Sheet

Key SAP Terms

TermWhat It Means
ABAPAdvanced Business Application Programming — SAP's proprietary programming language
ALVABAP List Viewer — SAP's standard grid/table display framework
BAPIBusiness Application Programming Interface — standardized API for SAP business objects
BTPBusiness Technology Platform — SAP's cloud platform
CDSCore Data Services — modern data modeling layer using SQL-like views
Clean ABAPSAP's official coding style guide for modern, readable ABAP
Clean CoreSAP's strategy for keeping S/4HANA upgrade-stable and cloud-compliant by extending — not modifying — the core, across six dimensions: software stack, extensibility, integrations, data, processes, operations
CAPCloud Application Programming Model — framework for building side-by-side extensions on SAP BTP
ATCABAP Test Cockpit — SAP's static analysis / code quality checks; used by AWS ABAP Accelerator to validate AI-generated code
ABAP AcceleratorOfficial AWS MCP server (2026) that connects Kiro to SAP via ADT + ATC for validated code generation, ECC→S/4HANA conversion, and clean core development
MCPModel Context Protocol — open standard that lets AI assistants connect directly to tools and data sources like SAP
Released APIAn SAP object officially released for consumption in extensions — a core principle of clean core
ECCERP Central Component — the older SAP ERP system (pre-S/4HANA)
RAPRESTful ABAP Programming Model — modern framework for building OData services
S/4HANASAP's current ERP suite running on HANA database
SAP ADTABAP Development Tools — the standard protocol and toolset for ABAP development
SE80 / SE38Classic SAP transactions for ABAP development (being replaced by ADT)

Prompt Starter Templates

Copy any of these and paste into Kiro chat:

Quick Report
Write an ABAP report for S/4HANA that reads [TABLE] filtered by [FIELD] and displays results in an ALV grid using CL_SALV_TABLE. Use modern ABAP syntax.
Explain Code
Explain this ABAP code: what it does, any performance issues, and how to improve it.
Modernize Code
Refactor this ABAP code to Clean ABAP: inline declarations, no SELECT *, no SELECT in LOOP, use CL_SALV_TABLE, add error handling.
Fix Bugs
This ABAP code has bugs. Find all issues and provide a corrected version with explanations.

Prompts by SAP Module (FI · SD · MM)

Module-anchored starters — each prefers released CDS views (clean core) with the classic tables as a fallback. Add the ABAP Accelerator line ("then create and activate the objects in my SAP system and run ATC until clean") if you are connected.

FI — Financial Accounting
Write an ABAP report for S/4HANA (FI) that reads G/L line items from the ACDOCA universal journal (or the released I_JournalEntryItem CDS view) for a company code and fiscal-year range, and displays document number, posting date, G/L account, amount, and currency in an ALV grid using CL_SALV_TABLE. Prefer released APIs and use modern ABAP syntax (inline declarations, string templates).
SD — Sales and Distribution
Write an ABAP report for S/4HANA (SD) that reads sales orders from the released I_SalesOrder / I_SalesOrderItem CDS views (or VBAK/VBAP) filtered by sales organization and creation date, and shows sales order, item, material, order quantity, net value, and sold-to party in CL_SALV_TABLE. Follow Clean ABAP naming and use inline declarations.
MM — Materials Management
Write an ABAP report for S/4HANA (MM) that reads purchase orders from the released I_PurchaseOrder / I_PurchaseOrderItem CDS views (or EKKO/EKPO) filtered by company code and document date, joined to material master (MARA), and displays purchase order, item, material, quantity, net price, and supplier in CL_SALV_TABLE with modern ABAP syntax.
Unit Test — SD/FI pricing and tax class
Generate ABAP Unit tests for an SD/FI pricing-and-tax class that computes net value (quantity x unit price) and country tax (DE 19%, US 8%, JP 10%, otherwise 15%): risk level harmless, use CL_OSQL_TEST_ENVIRONMENT test doubles for the VBAP / pricing data access, and cover positive, negative, and boundary cases (zero quantity, unknown country, 100% discount) with setup and teardown methods.
